ASPIRE updates existing posterior samples into the posterior under a new hypothesis without restarting from the prior. It combines normalising flows with a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to produce accurate posteriors and unbiased evidence estimates. Applying ASPIRE to a number of dark siren analysis cases with GWTC-5.0, we recover posteriors consistent with nested sampling, while recording a performance improvement of between 6-28 times over the set of analyses when using an existing posterior. This enables efficient exploration of modelling choices and rapid updates as catalogs grow, without duplicating existing computational effort.

papers.t: Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach
papers.abs: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 17 figures

papers.t: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $Λ$CDM simulations
papers.abs: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $Λ$CDM expectations.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ on 17-10-2026. 30 pages, 12 figures, 8 tables

papers.t: Solar models using OPLIB monochromatic opacities
papers.abs: Context. Opacity is a key ingredient in describing the transport of energy in stars. There are several methods for calculating stellar opacities, resulting in different tables (OPAL, OP, OPAS, and OPLIB). These opacities are available in two distinct forms: tables that regroup the Rosseland mean opacity pre-calculated at predefined chemical mixtures, and monochromatic opacity spectra of individual chemical elements, which allow for the computation of Rosseland mean opacity for a precise mixture. Aims. This study presents our implementation of the OPLIB monochromatic opacity data in Cesam2k20 and compares the solar-calibrated model obtained with these opacities to helioseismic data in order to evaluate the improvements made by using monochromatic opacities. Methods. We implemented the OPLIB monochromatic opacity data in the Cesam2k20 stellar evolution code following the method already used for the OP monochromatic opacity data. Results. We found that calibrated solar models produced with monochromatic opacity data (OP and OPLIB) agree better overall with helioseismic constraints than those produced with pre-calculated opacity tables.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.abs: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the strongest and most efficient jet, as it accumulates the most magnetic flux at the black hole horizon. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $σ\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $Γ_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 18 figures, submitted to MNRAS

papers.t: Residual ellipticity driven by intense magnetic stress in the hot neutron star era
papers.abs: A neutron star with a nonaxisymmetric mass distribution continuously radiates gravitational waves. The amplitude depends on the magnitude of the deformation, and is crucial for gravitational-wave astronomy. We studied an evolutionary effect on the magnetically induced ellipticity in the neutron star crust. A large deformation at the hot era before solidification is assumed to be produced magneto-hydrodynamically, and the fate at later time follows owing to the decrease in the force associated with the decay and redistribution of the current. Instead of simulating the evolution of deformation with the magnetic field over a long timescale, we estimate the ellipticity that remains after the formation of the solid crust by comparing two equilibrium models before and after solidification. The relic ellipticity is $\sim 10^{-8} (B_0/10^{13}{\rm{G}})^2$ in the magnitude for dipole field strength $B_{0}$ at the surface. This value was primarily determined by the magnetic field at the later time, with a weak dependence on the initial large deformation. The memory of the presolidification state was retained, but was small because the elastic force contributes little to the equilibrium.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures

papers.t: Validating Updated Precession and Nutation Formulations for the Next IERS Conventions
papers.abs: An international effort via the IAU/IAG Joint Working Group on Consistent Improvement of Earth's Rotation Theory (CIERT) aims to update the nutation theory to meet the milliarcsecond accuracy required by GGOS. While a companion article provides the theoretical background to the proposed precession-nutation corrections, this work presents their VLBI-based observational validation. The analysis systematically evaluates the revised models within practical application in VLBI analysis. These results provide critical empirical input for the upcoming integration of consistent, validated Earth rotation models into the next IERS Conventions.

papers.t: Kinessence, phantom crossing and sign-switching dark energy
papers.abs: We introduce Kinessence models where combining K-mouflage and quintessence leads to phantom-crossing of the dark energy equation of state and sign-switching of the dark energy density. This is realised by joining a dark scalar sector comprising K-essence kinetic terms and a quintessence potential together with a Yukawa coupling to matter. We investigate the dynamics of these models in the Jordan frame at the background and perturbative levels. We concentrate on the effective equation of state and the matter fraction for the background. The CMB spectra, the linear power spectrum and the growth of structure via $fσ_8$ are also analysed at the perturbative level. The quintessence potential drives the acceleration of the Universe at low redshift with an equation of state greater than -1. The Yukawa coupling to matter leads to a phantom crossing behaviour depending on its strength. The potential fifth force mediated by the scalar field is screened by the K-mouflage mechanism triggered by the K-essence kinetic terms and passes Solar System tests. This allows for relatively large Yukawa couplings to matter $β\sim 0.1$, large enough to lead to the crossing of the phantom divide at $z\sim 0.5$. Despite a significant scalar interaction on large scales, we find that the growth of structure is reduced compared to LCDM. The matter fraction deviates from the standard model by a few percent and the Hubble rate is larger at low redshift than at recombination whilst the CMB spectra show small deviations from LCDM. The dark energy fraction becomes negative at redshifts greater than 2. All these features should alleviate the various tensions such as the larger value of $H_0$ at small redshift, a possible reduction of growth as measured by $S_8$ and the bound on the sum of the neutrino masses. Deviations from LCDM of the CMB lensing spectrum may provide a detectable window for these models.
papers.comment: 48 pages, 27 figures

papers.t: Revisiting the Isospin Quartic Term of the Nucleonic Matter Equation of State in the Walecka Model
papers.abs: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(ρ_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.
papers.comment: 32 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables

papers.t: Dissecting and diagnosing the LISA Galactic binary population
papers.abs: LISA will individually resolve thousands of Galactic double white dwarf (DWD) binaries, while the majority stays buried in an unresolved gravitational wave (GW) confusion foreground. Which systems get resolved depends on the binary's parameters, on the global population and on instrumental sensitivity, so the resolved population is not a representative sample of the underlying Galactic population. Interpreting LISA's future catalog therefore requires understanding these selection effects. Here we characterize the resolved and unresolved subpopulations of a simulated Milky Way DWD catalog, using an iterative subtraction pipeline applied over different observation times. Resolvability is driven primarily by chirp mass: higher chirp mass, inspiraling systems are strongly favored over lower mass, outspiraling or monochromatic ones, and this reflects on the rate with which different composition subtypes are resolved. Spatially, resolved sources trace the Galactic bulge, because it is intrinsically the densest region of the Galaxy. The confusion background shows an internal bimodal chirp-mass structure, and is not generated uniformly by the same subpopulation in different frequency bands. We introduce a diagnostic for the minimum number of sources needed to reproduce a given fraction of the confusion power in a frequency band, and show that a residual confusion floor persists even after 100 years of integration. These biases are significant and need to be accounted for when using LISA's resolved DWD catalog and the confusion background to constrain the Galactic DWD population.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 15 figures

papers.t: Metadata for the Flux Density Calibration of the April 2021 and March 2022 Event Horizon Telescope Science Data
papers.abs: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has been conducting science observations annually since 2021 after the initial campaigns in 2017 and 2018. In this memo, we report on the metadata associated to the observations from 2021 April and 2022 March at 1.3mm wavelengths. We follow a similar path for the collection, processing, and validation of the metadata used for the initial amplitude calibration of the 2018 EHT data. In this release, we introduce some differences regarding the treatment of sensitivities and gain curves for some stations. In addition, we describe the changes to the EHT array since 2018.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 5 figures, EHT Memo Series 2026-L1-01

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) Euclid photometric masks
papers.abs: This paper describes the Euclid DR1 photometric masks, which trace spatial variations in the survey properties (e.g. satellite position angles, integration time, sky tiling, and survey footprint); in the instrumental performance of Euclid and the external data (EXT) it uses (e.g. survey coverage, depth, PSF width, quality flags, systematic effects and astrometric uncertainties); and in possible contamination from sky emission (e.g. galactic extinction and zodiacal light emission). Among this, the effective coverage mask is particularly important as it defines the effective survey area and can be used to exclude spurious objects when selecting Euclid photometric samples for scientific analyses. The Euclid photometric masks are built for each observed sky region (tile) and are provided as full-sky HEALPix maps (nested ordering and explicit indexing) at Nside = 16 384, equating to a resolution of 12"88, for both the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Euclid Deep Survey (EDS). We estimate the total area of the DR1 EWS (EDS) to be 2008.8 (74.7) deg$^2$ and find that 82 (81)\% of this area is preserved by the effective coverage mask. We observe that Euclid's instrumental properties are consistent with expectations, showing only minor relative variations across the sky. For DR1 EWS the standard deviation of the depth (computed for a 2" aperture and at 5 $σ$) is below 0.2 AB mag, with median values of 25.69, 24.14, 24.3, and 24.29 for the Euclid IE, YE, JE, and HE bands. Finally, we expect these photometric masks to be key to many science applications and in particular for cosmological analyses.

papers.t: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
papers.abs: Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}δ_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band ($g,r,i,z,y$) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: $σ_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.020$ for $z$, $0.169\,\mathrm{dex}$ for $\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $0.073$ for $D_n4000$, and $1.185\,\text{Å}$ for $\mathrm{H}δ_A$. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (RMSE changes $\le 3.5\%$) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, accepted by A&A

papers.t: Direct estimation of the lunar-solar precession with geodetic very long baseline interferometry
papers.abs: Geodetic very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) is capable of measuring the Earth's instantaneous rotation pole (IRP) components (hereafter, $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$) with sufficient accuracy using the VLBI delay rate. The least-squares fit of the $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$ polynomial expansion coefficients produces the precession model parameters independently of planetary motion theories. Our aim was to estimate the precession parameters using VLBI delay rate observations as well as the nutation coefficients in order to produce a full transformation matrix from the IRP to the Geocentric Celestial Reference System (GCRS). Then, the goal was to incorporate the free core nutation (FCN) effect from the VLBI group delay to form a complete and simple analytical model. We obtained an empirical model of the transformation from International Terrestrial Reference System (ITRS) to Geocentric Celestial Reference System (GCRS) based on observational results. Similar to the IAU2006 theory, the new model produces time series of $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$ angles, but these two angles now point out the direction of the IRP rather than the celestial intermediate pole (CIP). A simple analytical model defines the IRP location for any epoch during the interval of observations. Therefore, the non-rotation origin concept is not required for the transformation matrix construction. The estimate of the lunar-solar precessional parameter based on analysis of VLBI delay rate is $ψ_{A}= 5038.500\pm 0.019"$/cy (referred to the observational epoch 2000.0), which is close to the adopted IAU2006 precessional parameter value $ψ_{A}= 5038.4815"$/cy.
papers.comment: 10 pages, accepted for publication

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Spacecraft performance in the L2 environment
papers.abs: The Euclid mission was designed around the need for thermo-optical and mechanical stability, stray-light suppression, low outgassing, and precise guiding. After three years in space, a wealth of data is available to assess the performance in these areas. We review the L2 halo-orbit design and consumables budget. Solar stray-light gradually increases by 14\% per year and is consistent with meteoroid puncturing, but remains low overall. Data loss from high solar activity has declined notably since the maximum of the 25th Solar cycle passed. The thermodynamical response of the optical elements to a thermal step impulse follows sigmoidal growth curves, entering the asymptotic equilibration regime after 21--46 hours. Water-ice contamination has affected data from both instruments and requires continued monitoring; we review detection and decontamination methods, and Euclid's contamination history. High-precision measurements of the zodiacal background reveal, at eight sigma significance, the subtle modulation caused by the changing perspective on the dust distribution due to the L2 halo-orbit libration. These data also show that conservative pre-launch estimates overestimated the out-of-field stray-light by factors of 4 (H band) to 27 (I band). Telemetry data demonstrate excellent guiding, and enable highly significant detections of solar radiation pressure and of thermal-emission recoil from Euclid's unilluminated dark sides. Lastly, we present a list of 34 meteoroid impacts, discuss their mechanical and optical signatures, and derive a minimum detectable impactor mass of 5e-7 g.
papers.comment: 38 pages, 33 figures; companion paper of Euclid DR1

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Calibration strategy and observations
papers.abs: This paper reviews how Euclid's top-level calibration requirements were translated into a calibration plan, how this plan is implemented and maintained during the survey, and how it performs in the current DR1 release. We show that DR1 already meets or exceeds most end-of-mission spectrophotometric calibration requirements. The construction of spectroscopically complete and pure samples relies on ongoing data acquisition for the Euclid Deep Survey, while point-spread-function modelling and shear calibration are still converging to their stringent accuracy requirements. With all DR1 data reprocessed with the DR1 pipeline configuration, more subtle effects have been detected and characterised, and correction strategies have been developed for DR2. These include improved absolute flux calibration, astrometry, charge-persistence correction, shutter effects, wavelength calibration, and spectrophotometric corrections for water-ice contamination. Finally, synthetic photometric transformations between Euclid and each of Roman, the James Webb Space Telescope, and the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope, are presented.
papers.comment: 43 pages, 17 figures; companion paper of Euclid DR1

papers.t: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
papers.abs: In this work, we apply Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to the Chandra Source Catalog (CSC) to investigate the distribution of observation-level detections in the feature space defined by their spectral and variability properties. SOMs are neural-network-based models that project points in high-dimensional space onto a two-dimensional latent space while preserving their local topological structure. From CSC 2.1.1 we extract a sample of 36,904 ACIS-only, observation-level, high statistical significance detections, belonging to 17,927 unique sources. Among these detections, 25,192 (10,078 sources) are associated with a label from SIMBAD via a 1" cross-match that provides information about their astrophysical nature. Training a 40x40 hexagonal SOM reveals structured regions in the U-Matrix and activation response map, and feature-projection maps trace coherent patterns in spectral shape and variability. Overlaying SIMBAD classes shows that labeled populations occupy distinct, partially adjacent regions of the map and that generic categories can be interpreted via their SOM locations. We then retrain the SOM for classification using a source-grouped train/validation/test split and introduce SOMClassifier. When applied to 11,712 detections without SIMBAD labels, it assigns valid (non-abstained) labels to 6,225 detections (coverage ~53%). Furthermore, we release the trained models and visualization/classification workflows through a public web application built on the most up-to-date CSC release.
papers.comment: 34 pages, 19 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Colouring Euclid with external ground-based imaging data
papers.abs: Accurate photometric-redshift estimation and calibration of the weak-lensing point-spread function (PSF) for Euclid require complementary ground-based optical imaging with high photometric precision and spatial homogeneity. The Organisation Unit for External Data (OU-EXT) integrates heterogeneous ground-based surveys into the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), delivering uniformly calibrated, co-added images, and associated PSF models. To minimise systematics in spectral energy distribution (SED) reconstruction and photometric-redshift estimation, these data must achieve relative photometric stability at the $\sim$10 mmag level on Euclid-tile scales. We present the ground-based imaging component of Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), comprising $\sim2500$ deg$^2$ across the wide, deep, and auxiliary fields. We summarise the OU-EXT production workflow and validation framework, and quantify the achieved data quality of the co-added products in terms of depth, photometric zero-point stability, and spatial colour homogeneity. In the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS), the point-source $10σ$ depths in the $griz$ bands reach 24.8/24.3/24.0/23.0 AB mag, with the deep fields extending 1--2 magnitudes deeper. Most EWS DR1 tiles meet the 10 mmag relative photometric requirement, with 1.1% and 1.5% showing offsets exceeding 50 mmag in the northern and southern hemispheres, respectively. Spatial colour variations remain typically below 5--10 mmag across the southern EWS footprint, while larger residual structures of 10--25 mmag appear in some northern regions. These results demonstrate that the EXT production chain provides a largely homogeneous framework for integrating ground-based datasets into Euclid, while identifying calibration and co-addition limitations that have to be addressed in DR2 to meet the mission's most stringent cosmological requirements. (Abridged)
papers.comment: 27 pages, 21 pages. Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''

papers.t: Euclid First Data Release 1 (DR1) - Data release overview
papers.abs: This paper describes the contents of the Euclid First Data Release (DR1), together with the set of papers that document the data-processing and the data products. DR1 consists of two parts: first `DR1-Foundation', releasing images, spectra, and catalogues in November 2026. Second, the shear measurements and the `Level~3' products required for cosmological analyses will be added in June 2027 to complete the full DR1. This data set contains around a billion catalogued objects, mainly from the Euclid Wide Survey (1975\,deg$^2$) and the Euclid Deep Fields (77\,deg$^2$)
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue 'Euclid First Data Release'. 11 pages, 4 figures

papers.t: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
papers.abs: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$α$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$α$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$α$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$α$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$α$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}α}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''. 18 pages, 15 figures

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) - NISP-P point-spread function modelling pipelines
papers.abs: The images collected in photometric mode by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) instrument of the Euclid satellite are used to model the point-spread function (PSF) of a selection of sources detected in single and combined frames. We used Q1 and DR1 data to improve the development of the PSF module of the near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) and to refine the models currently provided. We explored a few methods normally used to evaluate the quality of the derived models and discuss possible variations related to the position of the sources in the focal plane and to the wavelength and time of the observations. The procedure of fitting the PSF profile, compared to other methods used for flux estimation, such as aperture photometry, indicates that updated models are better than those provided by Q1 images. The current results are in agreement with several key requirements defined for the mission, but there is still room for further improvements, which we plan to investigate and implement in future releases.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 16 figures, Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''

papers.t: The Black Hole Mass of the Sunflower Galaxy NGC 5055: Direct Measurement via Stellar Kinematics with Keck/OSIRIS Laser Guide Star Adaptive Optics
papers.abs: We present the first stellar-dynamical supermassive black hole mass measurement in the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 5055 (M63) using near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with Keck/OSIRIS assisted by the laser guide star adaptive optics system. The observations deliver two-dimensional stellar kinematics extracted from the CO bandhead absorption features via pPXF at an angular resolution of $0.045''$. The stellar velocity dispersion rises steeply from $\sim90~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$ at $r\sim1''$ to a central peak of $\sim135~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$, kinematically tracing the gravitational influence of a central mass concentration. Modeling these kinematics with an ensemble of four JAM models, spanning cylindrical and spherical velocity-ellipsoid alignments and two independent MGE decompositions of archival HST imaging, yields a black hole mass of $M_{\rm BH}=4.56^{+1.73}_{-1.82}\times10^6~{\rm M_\odot}$. The stellar orbits are consistent with near-isotropy ($β\approx0$), typical of rotating late-type galaxies. NGC 5055 emerges as a remarkable local analogue to the Milky Way in terms of its black hole, nuclear star cluster, and total stellar mass. The surface brightness profile of NGC 5055 shows no evidence for a classical bulge; if confirmed bulgeless, NGC 5055 would join the rare class of spirals with a direct dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ determination in the absence of a bulge, a regime currently populated by only a handful of galaxies including NGC 2748 and NGC 4395. This measurement provides a new anchor for black hole scaling relations in late-type galaxies at the low-mass end of the black hole mass spectrum.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables; accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NIR astrometric calibration
papers.abs: This paper presents the methodology and results of the astrometric calibration applied to the Euclid Near-Infrared (NIR) images in the Euclid Data Release 1, focusing on the techniques used to model and correct instrumental distortions, as well as the assessment of calibration quality. This work details the calibration pipeline, including quality control tests, and the evaluation of astrometric residuals against the Gaia DR3 catalogue and internal consistency metrics based on data encompassing more than one year of Euclid operation: the achieved accuracy is 30 mas for 97% of the total area, thus exceeding the requirements for Data Release 1. For the remaining 3%, accuracy declines due to a persistence correction issue: a method to correct the issue is presented. Furthermore, we discuss the stability of the solution over time, its dependence on source properties and instrument configuration, and outline the improvements planned for future Euclid data releases to enhance the astrometric calibration accuracy and efficiency.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''(12 pages, 12 figures)

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). An overview of the Science Ground Segment architecture and operations
papers.abs: The Euclid mission is designed to address fundamental questions on the nature of dark energy and dark matter by mapping the extragalactic sky with a wide-area survey complemented by targeted deep observations. The required scientific performance places stringent demands on the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), which transforms raw telemetry into calibrated, validated, and scientifically exploitable products. The SGS is a distributed system comprising the Euclid Science Operations Centre, the Science Data Centres, Instrument Operation Teams, and supporting Organisation Units, within a common architectural and procedural framework. This paper presents the SGS as implemented for Data Release 1 (DR1), describing its organisation, architecture, processing functions, and operational model. We outline the main components of the SGS common infrastructure. A key element is the Euclid Archive System (EAS), the central metadata repository based on a common data model. It comprises a Distributed Storage System, providing scalable storage of data files across the Science Data Centres; a Data Processing System used by the pipelines to register and access files and their lineage; and a Science Archive, distributing validated data products. Processing is coordinated by a common orchestration framework based on the Infrastructure Abstraction Layer, providing workflow management and resource abstraction of distributed compute clusters. Software development, integration, and deployment are supported by the Common Development Environment. We describe daily operations, calibration, and quality control, followed by the DR1 production campaign, including processing flows, validation strategy, and computational and data volumes. This infrastructure enabled Euclid DR1, involving 35 million jobs across nine Science Data Centres and 6.7 million core-hours, demonstrating robustness and scalability of the SGS.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release'', 25 pages, 12 figures

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The PHZ processing function for the physical properties of galaxies
papers.abs: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures. Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''

papers.t: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
papers.abs: We develop a scattering-order-resolved Stokes-vector recursion for axisymmetric polarized transport in a finite plane-parallel Thomson slab. The post-scattering radiation field closes exactly within two depth-dependent coefficients, yielding escape probabilities, angular distributions and linear polarization while conserving photon number. At high scattering orders, the principal eigenmode of the weighted self-adjoint transport operator controls the escape statistics, and the normalized angular distribution and polarization become independent of the seed source. The subdominant spectrum quantifies convergence, with the characteristic scattering order scaling as the square of the optical depth in thick slabs. We derive logarithmic corrections to the thin-slab complete-polarization limit away from the slab normal, together with a finite-optical-depth Galerkin approximation. In optically thick slabs, matching bulk diffusion to a polarized Milne surface layer yields finite-thickness corrections to the Chandrasekhar solution. We provide compact formulae for the principal and leading subdominant eigenvalues and the asymptotic angular and polarization distributions across both regimes. Combining the recursion with an angle-averaged thermal-Compton redistribution kernel gives approximate energy-resolved Stokes spectra. Comparisons with full polarized Compton calculations show that this separable reconstruction is most reliable for cool, optically thick media. Applied to the non-dipping observations of neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary system 4U 1624-49, the model provides acceptable joint fits to the broadband intensity and IXPE Stokes spectra, showing that an extended corona overlying the accretion disc can account for the observed X-ray polarization.
papers.comment: 34pages, 16 figures, submitted to MNRAS

papers.t: EP250226a: A fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A and its multiwavelength afterglow properties
papers.abs: Recent advances in fast X-ray transient studies have been driven by the wide-field, sensitive soft X-ray monitoring capabilities of the Einstein Probe (EP), enabling the prompt detection and localization of previously underexplored events. EP observations offer new opportunities to investigate the origins, emission mechanisms, and population properties of newly discovered fast X-ray transients. We present multiwavelength observations of EP250226a, an extragalactic fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A. We jointly analyze the prompt emission from soft X-rays to gamma rays and the X-ray afterglow spectra. We collect optical photometric data, perform empirical and afterglow model-based analyses, and present optical-to-infrared spectroscopy, measuring the equivalent widths of absorption lines. The spectroscopic redshift is $z = 3.314$, and the isotropic-equivalent gamma-ray energy is $E_\mathrm{iso}\simeq7.32\times10^{53}$ erg. Its location in the Amati diagram is consistent with a massive-star core-collapse origin (Type II GRB). The fluence ratio $\rm{S}(25-50\,\rm{keV})/\rm{S}(50-100\,\rm{keV})=0.57\pm0.06$ supports its classification as a classical GRB. The X-ray and optical afterglows show achromatic behavior. Among the models considered, a top-hat jet propagating into a uniform interstellar medium best describes the multiwavelength afterglow. This model suggests a highly collimated, nearly on-axis jet, with an isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of $E_\mathrm{k,iso}\simeq4.07\times10^{55}$ erg, a gamma-ray radiative efficiency of $η_γ\simeq 1.77\%$, and a low magnetic-field energy fraction of $\log ε_\mathrm{B,FS} \simeq -6.52$. EP250226a exhibits typical long-duration GRB properties, with the first soft X-ray peak coinciding with the gamma-ray prompt emission, while the soft X-ray emission lasts significantly longer than the gamma-ray emission.
papers.comment: 32 pages, 17 figures, and 5 tables. The revised manuscript has been submitted to A&A

papers.t: Minimal vacuum histories beyond $Λ$CDM: model comparison within VCDM
papers.abs: Recent cosmological observations motivate alternatives to $Λ$CDM with evolving dark energy. We compare three such models, each introducing one additional cosmological parameter: F42, with equation of state $w(a)=w_0/\sqrt{a}$, and two smooth sign-changing effective dark-energy profiles, Ag and Qui. All models are implemented within VCDM, which determines the background and linear perturbations without introducing an additional propagating gravitational degree of freedom. We use CMB observations from SPT, Planck, and ACT, combined with DESI DR2 distance measurements, with and without the DESY5 Dovekie supernova sample. All three alternatives improve the best-fit likelihood relative to $Λ$CDM. When supernovae are included, the Akaike information criterion favors F42, while Ag and Qui remain nearly indistinguishable from $Λ$CDM on this criterion. The Bayesian evidence, however, does not establish a robust preference among the three alternatives. Our results show that improved fits to current observations can arise from physically different dark-energy histories, motivating complementary measurements of expansion and structure growth to distinguish them.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables; corrected name of author

papers.t: Stellar Loci XI: Identifications and Parameter Determinations of Binary Stars by multi-band photometry
papers.abs: Large photometric surveys contain numerous unresolved binaries, but identifying them and measuring component properties remains challenging. We present a 65-band UV-to-IR SED-fitting framework to identify unresolved main-sequence binaries and infer their parameters. Photometry combines synthetic miniJPAS magnitudes from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra with 2MASS and WISE measurements. Using LAMOST-calibrated, metallicity-dependent stellar loci and a dwarf-star color-absolute-magnitude relation, we construct forward models for single stars and unresolved binaries. We fit both model families to each SED with MCMC, using Gaia distances as Hertzsprung-Russell-diagram constraints to infer metallicity, reddening, and component photometric parameters. Component masses and mass ratios are derived from PARSEC models. Simulations show the method robustly recovers binary parameters. Tests on a LAMOST comparison sample indicate sensitivity to binaries with $q\gtrsim0.4$; the preferred model reproduces spectroscopic metallicities with 0.11 dex scatter, while inferred reddenings agree with external extinction maps with $\sim0.02$ mag scatter. Comparison with an external Gaia XP-based binary catalog shows broadly consistent binary classifications for common sources. Our metallicities more closely follow the LAMOST spectroscopic scale, and mass-ratio estimates in the intermediate-$q$ regime better trace expected $Δ$-HRD offsets. Tests using M67 members support internal consistency of inferred parameters. For quality-selected Gaia non-single-star binaries, primary-mass estimates agree with Gaia NSS values with 0.071 $M_\odot$ residual scatter; in cases with larger discrepancies, further tests indicate that secondary-mass and mass-ratio estimates are more reliable than the Gaia NSS values. The method scales to large photometric samples, enabling population studies and analyses of individual systems.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 23 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJS

papers.t: Exceptional point excitation by a plunging particle
papers.abs: We investigate the excitation of a second-order exceptional point (EP) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum by a plunging particle. Starting from a gravitational action, we derive the master equation with a Gaussian bump modified potential. For the odd-parity mode $(\ell,m)=(2,1)$, we compute the waveform numerically and derive an analytic expression for the EP contribution to the ringdown waveform directly from the particle source. Comparison with the numerical waveform shows that the particle excites the EP response, which, together with its mirror contribution, dominates the intermediate ringdown stage. We use waveform fitting and Bayesian analysis to assess the limitations of conventional QNM templates for EP ringdown. In the fitting, the EP template recovers the complex frequency $ω$ more accurately than the ordinary template. In Bayesian analysis, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $ρ=100$, the ordinary template yields a narrow frequency posterior whose $90\%$ credible region excludes the true EP frequency, whereas the broader EP-template region contains it. The Bayes factor nevertheless favors the ordinary template at lower SNRs and the EP template only at higher SNRs. These results show that in the EP case a narrow posterior and favorable Bayesian evidence do not guarantee accurate frequency inference when a conventional template omits the characteristic EP ringdown structure.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 7 figures

papers.t: B-fields And Dust in InterstelLar FiLAments Using Dust POLarization (BALLAD-POL): V. Magnetic Fields and Grain Alignment Mechanisms in Serpens Main Using JCMT/POL-2 Polarization
papers.abs: We investigate magnetic fields ($B$-field) and grain alignment mechanisms in Serpens Main using 850 $μ$m dust polarization observations from JCMT/POL-2. We derive a map of $B$-field strength and calculate the mass-to-flux ratio and Alfvénic Mach number, suggesting the subdominance of $B$-fields over gravity but their dominance over turbulence. Fitting the Ricean mean model to the nondebiased polarization fraction ($P$) as a function of emission intensity ($I$) yields a slope $α= 0.68\pm0.01$, revealing depolarization. To understand its origins, we examine the dependence of $P$ on gas column density ($N({\rm H}_{2})$), dust temperature ($T_{\rm d}$), and polarization angle dispersion function ($S$). We find no correlation between $P$ and $S$, whereas for $P\times S$, an observational proxy for alignment efficiency decreases with increasing $N({\rm H}_{2})$. This suggests that $B$-field tangling is not the primary cause of depolarization and instead points to reduced grain alignment in denser regions. To test this interpretation within radiative torque (RAT) alignment theory, we calculate the minimum size of aligned grains ($a_{\rm align}$) and magnetic relaxation strength ($δ_{\rm mag,sp}$) using $N({\rm H}_{2})$, $T_{\rm d}$, and our estimated $B$-field map. We find that both $P$ and $P \times S$ decrease with increasing $a_{\rm align}$, supporting reduced grain alignment as the main cause of depolarization in Serpens Main. However, neither $P$ nor $P \times S$ shows a correlation with $δ_{\rm mag,sp}$, suggesting that enhanced grain alignment due to magnetic relaxation is insufficient to compensate for the reduced alignment associated with increasing $a_{\rm align}$ toward denser regions.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 22 Pages, 17 Figures

papers.t: Galaxy Clustering Topology in Observations and Cosmological Simulations
papers.abs: We present a genus topology analysis of the large-scale distribution of galaxies in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data (SDSS), comparing the observed topology with mock galaxy samples from the Horizon Run 4 (HR4) $N$-body simulation and four cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. We construct nine volume-limited samples and measure their genus curves at Gaussian smoothing scales of $4$--$12~h^{-1}{\rm Mpc}$. Overall, the modern galaxy models reproduce the observed genus statistics substantially better than the HGC, HOD, and SAM models examined by Choi et al. (2010). Among the models considered here, the HR4 Most-Bound-Halo Particle galaxy-assignment model shows somewhat better overall agreement with the SDSS topology than IllustrisTNG300 and FLAMINGO. The observed scale dependences of the genus shift parameter $Δν_f$ and void abundance parameter $A_V$ are somewhat steeper than those predicted by the simulations, but their joint discrepancy from HR4 is not statistically significant. The smaller-volume TNG100 and EAGLE realizations show significant excesses in $A_C$, at $4.5σ$ and $7.0σ$, respectively, relative to the observational uncertainties. When the expected cosmic variance of the simulations is taken into account, they do not necessarily indicate failures of the galaxy-formation prescriptions, but they caution that individual small-volume realizations may not be representative of the observed galaxy topology. Overall, modern galaxy formation models reproduce the observed topology substantially better than earlier models, while residual differences remain that can be tested more precisely with denser future surveys.
papers.comment: 11 pages,6 figures,3 tables

papers.t: 3D radiative transfer of K-series lines of He-like ions with SKIRT
papers.abs: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with XRISM has resolved line profiles of highly ionised ions, including P Cygni profiles, in many systems containing compact objects. To interpret these line profiles, forward modelling with three-dimensional radiative transfer (3D RT) calculations including the relevant ionic processes is required. Following our previous work on the Lyman-series lines of H-like ions, we present the implementation of the K-series lines of He-like ions with Z = 2-30 in the open-source Monte Carlo RT code SKIRT, providing a numerical tool for interpreting highresolution X-ray spectra of photoionised plasmas. Building upon the framework developed for H-like ions, we incorporate the resonance scattering (RS) and radiative recombination (RR) channels. We also implement the inner-shell ionisation (II) channel of Li-like ions for the production of He-like lines. We resolve fine-structure levels and account for level populations, frequency redistribution, phase function, and linear polarisation through transition-specific Mueller matrices. The implementation reproduces the expected RT effects in He-like lines. The Fe xxv w and y lines, dominated by the RS channel, develop optically thick line-profile distortions and P Cygni profiles in an outflowing plasma, whereas the x and z lines, dominated by the RR and II channels, do not exhibit such behaviour. The line intensities from the RS and RR channels agree well with Cloudy. The II channel further enhances the z line, which is not yet included in Cloudy. The linear polarisation calculations reproduce the analytical and experimental angular dependence of resonance scattering on a line-by-line basis. This extension to He-like lines, together with our previous implementation of H-like lines, enables 3D RT modelling of the major X-ray lines, providing a tool for constraining gas kinematics around compact objects observed with XRISM.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)

papers.t: C$_2$ Swan, CH and CN emission, surface temperature and luminous efficiency of the Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule from ground-based spectroscopy
papers.abs: The Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule entered the atmosphere over South Australia on 5 December 2020 at 12 km/s. A slitless spectral video, taken from the ground with a hand-tracked consumer camera, shows the capsule alone from 80 to 49 km. In the first ten seconds of heating the shock layer emits the CN violet system, the CH A-X band and the C$_2$ Swan bands, the latter for the first time in remote observations of a capsule entry. C$_2$ ($T_{\rm rot}\approx9200$ K, $T_{\rm vib}\approx7800$ K) and CN (about 7000 K) are far hotter than the surface. C$_2$ and CH disappear while the heat flux is still rising and CN persists, which we relate to the early pyrolysis of the carbon-phenolic ablator and to the changing boundary-layer chemistry. The colour temperature of the heat shield rises from 2720 to 3080 K, in agreement with airborne results. The radiated energy is one to two orders of magnitude below that of natural fireballs, because the light comes from the hot surface rather than from ablation vapour. A faint persistent train lights up about 1 s after the passage and fades within a few seconds, probably chemiluminescence in the cooling wake.
papers.comment: 42 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to Earth, Planets and Space. Data and movies: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24125212

papers.t: Machine-Learning Reconstruction of Intergalactic Medium Column-Density Maps from Observed Ly$α$ Emission Cubes
papers.abs: Understanding the large-scale structure of the intergalactic medium (IGM) is essential for studying galaxy evolution, particularly at $z \sim 2$--$6$, when cold filaments in the cosmic web are considered a primary mechanism for fueling galaxy growth. At these redshifts, Ly$α$ emission shifts into the optical regime and serves as the primary tracer of diffuse IGM for ground-based integral field units (IFUs). However, detections remain limited by low signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) and the complexities of resonant scattering. We present a proof-of-concept machine-learning framework to reconstruct IGM gas column-density maps from noisy Ly$α$ IFU emission cubes. Using Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) observations of $z \sim 2.3$ protoclusters as a case study, we train a custom convolutional neural network (CNN), the Column Density Estimator (CDE), on a simulated dataset combining IllustrisTNG100 with simplified radiative-transfer calculations and an approximate treatment of KCWI noise. The CDE successfully reconstructs broad filamentary structures in the simulated test set under these adopted assumptions. Applied to observed KCWI data, the CDE predicts gas column-density maps containing filamentary structures extending over $\gtrsim 40''$ ($\sim 1$ comoving Mpc), consistent with an IGM interpretation. The observed reconstructions remain conditional on the adopted models. These results illustrate the potential of the CDE framework for connecting diffuse Ly$α$ observations with simulations of the IGM.
papers.comment: 35 pages, 20 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)

papers.t: Self-Consistent Microscopic Description of the 146Sm Half-Life for Early Solar System Chronology
papers.abs: The extinct \textit{p}-process radionuclide $^{146}$Sm, decaying to $^{142}$Nd, is a key short-lived chronometer for the formation and early evolution of terrestrial planets and planetesimals. However, there has been a long-standing discrepancy in both the experimental measurements and the theoretical evaluations of the $^{146}$Sm half-life. To address this, a self-consistent microscopic framework for $α$ decay is developed in this work, in which the $α$ particle is treated as a four-nucleon quartet. Its formation amplitude in the nuclear interior is constructed from a coherent superposition of multiple pure single-particle configurations weighted by the pairing occupation amplitudes. Coupling this shell amplitude to the $α$ cluster that survives in the low-density surface region yields a self-consistently determined two-state (shell~$\oplus$~cluster) preformation weight and effective potential. The calculated half-lives for the neighboring emitters of $^{146}$Sm are in good agreement with the measured values. Cross-validation over the neighboring emitters reproduces each excluded half-life without any nucleus-specific adjustment, and yields $^{146}$Sm predictions consistent to within $\pm 6\%$ of the resulting half-life $T_{1/2}=75.1^{+6.1}_{-5.6}$~Ma. This provides a solid calibration for theoretical studies of the early solar system.

papers.t: Jet energetics and remnant magnetism in short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron-star mergers: A statistical study via broadband afterglow modeling
papers.abs: Short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs) are believed to originate from compact binary mergers, particularly binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, providing a probe of jet energetics and merger remnants. We compile broadband afterglow observations of 40 sGRBs and perform forward-shock modeling with off-axis Gaussian jets, excluding data potentially affected by additional energy injection. We derive distributions of beaming-corrected jet kinetic energy $E_k$ and radiative efficiency $η_γ$, and combine these with binary population synthesis and numerical simulations to infer remnant black hole (BH) magnetic fields assuming the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) jet-launching mechanism. For the 15 strictly constrained bursts, we find a median $E_k\simeq3.8\times10^{49}$ erg and $η_γ\simeq0.35$, with respective 68% intervals of $[5.1\times10^{48},1.9\times10^{50}]$ erg and [0.09, 0.79]. The inferred magnetic field supplied by the accretion disk and threading the BH horizon is approximately $7\times10^{15}$ G, with a 68% credible interval of $[2.3\times10^{15},2.4\times10^{16}]$ G, depending slightly on the neutron star equation of state. The full sample yields a higher median field of approximately $2\times10^{16}$ G, with the high-energy and high-field tails predominantly contributed by less well-constrained bursts. These results provide statistical constraints on sGRB jet energetics and suggest characteristic BH magnetic fields of order $10^{16}$ G. Comparison with pre-merger neutron star magnetic fields indicates a characteristic amplification factor of $η_B\sim10^3$, providing an observational constraint on magnetic field amplification during BNS mergers and subsequent BH formation.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 14 figures; accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: What the X-ray Emission from Young Supernovae Can Tell Us About Their Progenitors
papers.abs: We discuss constraints that the X-ray emission from supernovae can place on their progenitor stars. Since almost all X-ray supernovae arise from massive stars, we concentrate on implications for massive stars. These stars lose mass throughout their lifetime in the form of stellar winds. X-ray emission can be used to gauge the wind properties, especially the mass-loss rates, via various techniques. The abundance of various elements formed by nucleosynthesis within the stars, and released in the stellar explosion, can be estimated from X-ray spectra. In many cases, a combination of X-ray light curves and spectra can allow us to extricate the structure and morphology of the surrounding medium formed by pre-supernova mass loss into which the SN shock is expanding.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 9 Figures, Invited review for the Universe special issue "The Lifecycle of Massive Stars" editor Jacco van Loon. This manuscript has an up to date plot of observed X-ray SNe, with 140 X-ray SNe included. Please let me know of any I have missed

papers.t: Origin of the angular momentum of filaments in the local Universe
papers.abs: Velocity gradients compatible with rotation have been reported across certain nearby cosmic filaments. We show that rotational momentum might be generated in filaments in the local Universe in the presence of a cosmological constant (local dark energy) based on the theorem stating the general function for the equivalence of the gravitational field of a sphere and that of a point mass. We investigated how the cosmological constant modifies the finite-time acquisition and retention of angular momentum in an open filamentary core. Although its isotropic force exerts no direct axial torque, rotational motion can be seeded by tidal interactions with surrounding matter and incoming streams. Early tidal torques establish an imbalance in axial angular momentum, while the subsequent orbit crossing amplifies the resulting rotation, and ultimately, the cosmological constant is able to modify tidal-mode growth and finite-time angular momentum delivery.
papers.comment: 4 pages, A&A Lett., in press

papers.t: Local Intensity-based Correction for SMFT Longitudinal Magnetograms: Validation with SDO/HMI Observations
papers.abs: The Solar Magnetic Field Telescope (SMFT) at Huairou Solar Observing Station (HSOS) derives photospheric magnetic fields from single-wavelength Stokes measurements using a linear calibration based on the weak-field approximation. In sunspot umbrae, this linear approach systematically underestimates the true magnetic field strength---a well-known effect of magnetic underestimation. To mitigate this bias, we apply the Local Intensity-based Correction (LIC) as implemented in the standard HSOS data reduction procedure and validate its performance against SDO/HMI full-disk longitudinal magnetograms that are co-temporal and co-spatial with the SMFT observations for 26 active regions observed in 2019 and 2024. Pixel-level alignment between SMFT images ($992\times830$, $0.242^{\prime\prime}$~pixel$^{-1}$) and HMI snapshots ($4096\times4096$, $0.505^{\prime\prime}$~pixel$^{-1}$) is achieved using SIFT feature matching and RANSAC-based homography estimation, yielding inlier fractions of 40\% to 88\%. The LIC correction consistently improves the Pearson correlation coefficient $r$ with respect to HMI for all these 26 regions, with a mean improvement of $Δr = +0.041$ and a maximum of $Δr = +0.197$ for AR24114 (NOAA 13667). Residual discrepancies persist in the most severely underestimated pixels, highlighting an inherent limitation of any single-wavelength linear calibration. Nevertheless, our results demonstrate that the LIC correction is a robust and effective preprocessing step, and we recommend its routine application in quantitative analyses of SMFT longitudinal magnetograms.
papers.comment: 8 figures, 1 table, 11 pages

papers.t: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
papers.abs: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, submitted to PASP, data is available at https://zvar.caltech.edu

papers.t: Globular Clusters in the Time of JWST. II. Looks like the second, moves like the first: the syrphid-like intermediate population of NGC 2808
papers.abs: The present-day kinematics of multiple populations in globular clusters can retain information about their initial conditions and can therefore help trace how the different populations formed. We combine JWST and HST photometry and proper motions to study the internal dynamics of four populations in NGC 2808 out to about eight half-light radii: the first population (1P) and three second-population groups with increasing light-element processing (2Pa, 2Pb, and 2Pc), providing the first detailed kinematic characterisation of the chemically intermediate 2Pa. We find significant kinematic differences between the populations. While all four have similar sky-projected radial velocity dispersions, 2Pb and 2Pc have lower tangential dispersions than 1P and are strongly radially anisotropic, whereas 2Pa shares the only mildly anisotropic kinematics of 1P. Therefore, chemically distinct 2P groups have different dynamical properties, suggesting that they formed under different conditions and/or experienced a different subsequent dynamical evolution. In the outer JWST field, the velocity dispersion depends only weakly on stellar mass, with hints of inverted equipartition. The difference between radial and tangential equipartition is similar for 1P and 2Pa and decreases towards 2Pc, a trend that remains tentative given the uncertainties. Our results show that 2P is not a dynamically homogeneous group, and that the kinematics of its individual groups provide a key constraint for multiple population formation scenarios.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 12 figures, submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome

papers.t: MeerKAT and ASKAP EMU new radio-continuum observations of Wolf-Rayet nebula PCG 11 (Cohen's Ring)
papers.abs: We present new radio-continuum observations of the well-known Wolf-Rayet (WR) nebula PCG 11 (Cohen's Ring; named after and in honour of the co-author on the discovery paper, Martin Cohen) using observations from the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU), Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and MeerKAT surveys. We find that the elliptical shell surrounding Cohen's Ring has a flux density of 62$\pm$2\,mJy at 1000 MHz. The angular size of the elliptical emission is measured to be 54\arcsec$\times$45\arcsec\ (at P.A.=69.4\D), which agrees well with observations of the source in H$α$ and at 24\,$μ$m in the infrared. Using the measured angular size and a distance of 3.94$\pm$0.27\,kpc, we determine that the nebula has a linear size of $1.03(\pm0.07)\times0.86(\pm0.06)$\,pc. Together with our new and previously measured flux density estimates, we determine a spectral index for Cohen's Ring to be $α$=0.06$\pm$0.02, indicating that the emission from the WR nebula is of thermal origin. Based on a typical average expansion velocity of 75~km~s$^{-1}$ for a WR star with a Red Supergiant (RSG) progenitor, we estimate the age of Cohen's Ring to be $\sim$ 13500 years. Our NANTEN telescope CO observations suggest that Cohen's Ring was formed during a relatively recent mass-loss event, while the associated CO-emitting molecular gas reflects the cumulative effects of stellar-wind feedback over a much longer timescale ($\sim$1.5\,Myr). As one of the few WR ring nebulae with linked molecular gas, Cohen's Ring provides a valuable laboratory for studying the long-term impact of massive-star feedback on surrounding molecular clouds.
papers.comment: accepted for publication in the Serbian Astronomical Journal

papers.t: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
papers.abs: In a neutron star low-mass X-ray binary, heavy elements (with mass number ~100) are believed to be synthesized through the rapid-proton (rp) capture process, as indirectly indicated by the long tail of X-ray burst light curves. Although direct evidence for the rp-process was lacking so far, we reported in our previous study that an unidentified hump is present at ~30 keV of the Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 in its hard state. The feature was tentatively identified with a recombination quasi-continuum from highly ionized ions of cadmium or indium, which are possibly produced by the rp process during X-ray bursts and lifted up into the neutron-star atmosphere. To reinforce this scenario, we quantitatively evaluated the physical conditions of the assumed emitting region in the atmosphere, and confirmed that the scenario is possible when the putative rp-process ashes in the atmosphere has ~10^7 times higher abundances than their solar values. The results are compared with theoretical model calculations for the nucleosynthesis in X-ray bursts. We suggest that the observed spectral hump is a radiative recombination feature from the stable isotope 106Cd, produced in X-ray bursts via the rp-process. Further issues about the detectability are briefly discussed.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal; 11 pages with 5 figures

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Near-infrared processing and data products
papers.abs: The Euclid near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) converts the raw observations acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) into calibrated images and source-level products. Following the first implementation delivered with the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1), the NIR PF has been revised for the first major Euclid Data Release (DR1), with improvements to detector-level processing, calibration, image reconstruction, and quality control. The DR1 processing includes observations covering more than $1900\,\rm{deg}^2$ and has produced $71\,659$ calibrated near-infrared (NIR) images. We assess the performance of the processing chain through extensive astrometric and photometric validation. The astrometric solution reaches an average root-mean-square (RMS) of 10 mas, remaining below 20 mas for 99% of the dithers in all three NISP bands. Temporal variations in the instrumental throughput are typically corrected to a level of 2 mmag RMS, while the relative photometric accuracy reaches 0.9% for sources brighter than 19 mag in $Y_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}$, and $H_\mathrm{E}$, and the residual spatial variations of the photometric calibration across the focal plane are at the level of approximately 10 mmag for the entire sample. Despite some remaining limitations, the DR1 NIR imaging products are consistent with the required astrometric and photometric performance over the large area covered by this release.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 15 figures, submitted to A&A

papers.t: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
papers.abs: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to Sérsic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($μ_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release", submitted to A&A, 31 pages, 33 figures

papers.t: Dynamical stability of double planets in compact multiplanetary systems
papers.abs: The "peas-in-a-pod" architecture of planetary systems, where planets are roughly evenly sized and log-spaced, is pervasive throughout known exoplanetary systems. However, many systems deviate slightly from this trend in that they have a "gap" where no planet has been detected, where one might have otherwise expected one to exist. There are many common explanations for the existence of these gaps, including the existence of as-yet-undiscovered planets lurking in these gaps; however, we propose that one potential explanation for some of these gaps is that they are filled by binary planets, a pair of gravitationally bound planets orbiting a common center of mass outside of both bodies. Specifically, in this work, we investigate the dynamical stability of these binary planets as compared to the more conventionally assumed single planets using Monte Carlo N-body simulations. We find that binary planets are slightly less stable than single planets. Overall, we find that binary planets and their cousins in exomoons provide a plausible explanation, at least from a stability perspective, for the existence of some dynamical gaps.
papers.comment: Accepted by ApJ

papers.t: Desorption of water from cosmic silicates
papers.abs: Recent JWST and ALMA observations of protoplanetary disks have identified water reservoirs in the inner regions of the disks. This would provide terrestrial planets forming therein access to a water reservoir. In situ formation of water molecules on grain surfaces was proposed as one possible formation process in the PDS 70 system, but transport by small silicate particles coupled to the gas could be another mechanism. Laboratory experiments on the thermally induced desorption of water molecules from different water-containing silicates at elevated temperatures provide another possibility for the enrichment of water molecules in the inner disk. Physically and chemically bound water in silicates can be released upon annealing processes. Water that is physically bound undergoes desorption at temperatures up to 473 K. In contrast, chemically bound water in form of different silanol or Mg-OH groups in amorphous silicates or phyllosilicates, can be released at higher temperatures, ranging from 773 to 923 K. The relevant temperatures are sufficient to trigger the solid-state recrystallization of amorphous silicates to Mg-rich orthopyroxene and olivine. The existence of these crystalline silicates has been substantiated through Spitzer and JWST-MIRI observations. Based on the experimental results, we postulate that the desorption of bound hydroxyl groups may serve as a mechanism for the formation of the water reservoir at temperatures up to 900 K, much higher than the water sublimation temperature of 100 to 200 K.

papers.t: A Bright L4 Neptune Trojan Found by Stacking Archival ZTF Images
papers.abs: We report a Neptune Trojan found by a shift-and-stack search of archival Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) difference images of 2019 October, and recovered in public images of seven other telescopes back to 2008. The orbit uses 88 positions on 54 nights from 2008 to 2025, a 17.22-year arc, all measured on our own Gaia DR3 plate solutions. Its heliocentric osculating elements at JD 2460000.5 are a = 30.2158 +/- 0.0004 au, e = 0.0661 and i = 20.32 deg; a fit of the same positions with the independent orbit code Find_Orb agrees within 0.4 sigma in every element. The nominal orbit librates about Neptune's leading Lagrange point L4 with a period of 9.25 kyr and an amplitude of 8.7 deg over the next Myr, and 84 +/- 2% of 500 clones of the orbit remain L4 Trojans for 4.5 Gyr. Its absolute magnitude is H_V = 6.96 +/- 0.10 (linear phase law), or 6.81 +/- 0.06 on the H, G convention of the Minor Planet Center's list of Neptune Trojans, whose brightest L4 member has H = 7.26, so the object is possibly the brightest known L4 Neptune Trojan. Its color, g-r = 0.52 +/- 0.05, lies in the g-r range of the red Neptune Trojans, and for albedos of 0.05-0.15 its diameter is about 140-240 km.

papers.t: Crater Scaling Relationships for Gas Impingement on Planetary Regolith
papers.abs: Plume-surface interaction (PSI) effects remains a major uncertainty for operations on regolith-covered planetary bodies. Although spacecraft exhaust can erode surfaces, form craters, and accelerate ejecta, existing PSI relationships are largely derived for scenario-specific lunar and Martian landing conditions and are not yet reliably generalizable. Resolving this problem is important not only for spacecraft safety, but also because controlled thruster interactions could provide an active geotechnical experiment during asteroid reconnaissance. Measurements of thruster-formed craters and ejecta may constrain regolith density, strength, porosity, and particle properties that are otherwise difficult to determine remotely. Such information is particularly relevant to planetary defense, where uncertainty in near-surface properties can strongly affect the outcome of kinetic-impact mitigation and the interpretation of momentum transfer. We investigate gas-driven excavation using near-vacuum, pulsed-N$_2$ experiments in a cohesionless asteroid regolith analog and comparisons with a low-gravity drop-tower experiment and historical chemical-thruster tests.
