We adapt projectile-cratering $π$-scaling, and find that these relationships can describe gas crater volume as a function of gas, target, gravity, and nozzle properties. A common gravity-regime relationship describes the laboratory data and is consistent with an experimental low-gravity result. Generalizing the $π$-scaling relationship for cohesive targets shows consistency with Apollo-era chemical-thruster cases. These results provide a framework for using spacecraft thrusters as active geotechnical tools during small-body reconnaissance.
papers.comment: 45 pages, 12 figures, submitted to the Planetary Science Journal

papers.t: Magellan PFS Discovery of a Cold Gas Giant Exoplanet Likely Formed by a Gas Disk Gravitational Instability
papers.abs: Using the Planet Finder Spectrograph (PFS) on the 6.5-m Magellan Clay Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory we have discovered a cold gas giant exoplanet orbiting the K7V dwarf star HIP88962. 16 yrs of PFS observations imply an exoplanet with an orbital period of $\approx$ 19.3 yrs and a radial velocity semiamplitude (K) of 94.9 m s$^{-1}$. With a host star mass of 0.62 $M_\odot$, this implies a planet mass $M_p sin(i) \sim 5 M_{Jup}$. While stable M dwarfs have a PFS RMS of $\approx$ 3 m s$^{-1}$, the single Keplerian fit for HIP88962 has an RMS of $\approx$ 6 m s$^{-1}$, hinting at a second exoplanet. The best double planet Keplerian fit, with a 4.113 d period, still results in a RMS of $\approx$ 5 m s$^{-1}$. HIP88962 has Ca II H lines with twice the emission of four stable stars, implying that stellar activity may contribute to the RMS jitter error for the single Keplerian fit. When combined with Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry, HIP88962 b has a nearly edge-on orbit with inclination 91 $\pm$ 22 deg, true planet mass $4.83$ M$_{Jup}$, semimajor axis 6.15 $\pm$ 0.5 au, and eccentricity 0.718 $\pm$ 0.02. Including a PFS jitter of $\approx$ 7 m s$^{-1}$ yields $χ^2 = 0.995$ for the combined solution. A massive gas giant orbiting at $\approx$ 6 au around a 0.62 $M_\odot$ star is incompatible with published core accretion population synthesis models, but consistent with formation by gas disk gravitational instability.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, in press, ApJ Letters

papers.t: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
papers.abs: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, plus appendix

papers.t: Shear, vorticity, and $f(R)$ theories
papers.abs: We study how an extended spherical collapse model (ESCM), including shear, vorticity and chameleon screening, modifies the collapse threshold $δ_c(z)$ and $δ_c(M)$, the turnaround density $δ_t$, the turnaround radius $R_t$ and the halo mass function in the Hu-Sawicki $f(R)$ model, and whether these quantities can distinguish $f(R)$ from General Relativity (GR). Unlike the standard spherical collapse model (SSCM), in the ESCM $δ_c$ depends on mass, redshift and $|f_{R0}|$; we use it to compute the halo mass function with the excursion set approach. Between GR and the large-field (LF) limit of $f(R)$, $δ_c$ differs by a few percent within the ESCM and by about 20% between GR in the ESCM and the LF limit in the SSCM; $δ_t$ differs by about 27-29% and $R_t$ by about 6.5%. With screening, the difference between GR and screened $δ_c$ is 2.5% for $|f_{R0}|=10^{-4}$ (F4) and vanishes for $|f_{R0}|=10^{-6}$ (F6); for $δ_t$ it is larger than 20% (F4), about 10% (F5) and 0 (F6); for $R_t$ about 6.5% (F4), 3% (F5) and 0 (F6). Since observations exclude F4 and F6 is practically identical to GR, only F5 could discriminate, but the ~20% uncertainty on measured turnaround radii rules out $R_t$ and related quantities as tests of $f(R)$. The halo abundance predicted by $f(R)$, especially at high redshift, can instead distinguish $f(R)$ from GR.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 9 figures. Published in Phys. Rev. D

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Pushing back the borders of the invisible with Euclid. Discovery of fifteen resolved low-surface-brightness stellar systems from the Milky Way to the Local Volume
papers.abs: We searched within the first data release of the Euclid Wide Survey (~1900 deg^2) for resolved stellar systems between distances from 10 kpc and several Mpc, using an isochrone filtering technique. We detect 15 systems that have never been resolved into stars before. Five are new discoveries, three in the Milky Way halo and two beyond the Local Group. The remaining ten are dwarf galaxies that were previously catalogued as unresolved sources in shallower ground-based surveys and lack reliable distance measures. We measured distance moduli for all 15 systems, and half-light radii, ellipticities, position angles, absolute magnitudes, and stellar masses for 14 of them. In the Milky Way halo, Ursa Minor II, at ~20 kpc, has Mv ~ +2.0 and a stellar mass of ~40 Msun, and is one of the least luminous stellar systems known. Fornax 7 is located near the tidal limit of the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy and may be physically associated with it. Eridanus V lies at ~165 kpc and has a stellar mass of ~550 Msun, which places it in the region of the size-luminosity plane where globular clusters and ultra-faint dwarf galaxies overlap. Beyond the Local Group, the 12 dwarf galaxies lie at distances of 3--5.5 Mpc. Three of them reach or exceed a mean surface brightness within the half-light radius of mu_V~28 mag/arcsec^2, a regime in which almost no galaxies at these distances were previously known. Ten of them are candidate members of the M81 group: eight have three-dimensional distances from M81 smaller than or comparable to the radius of its zero-velocity surface, and two lie close to the peripheral member NGC 4236, one of which is a candidate satellite of this galaxy. These results demonstrate Euclid's transformative potential for low-surface-brightness science, enabling the study of an unprecedented range of environments from the MW halo out to the Local Volume within a single, homogeneous survey.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 9 figures, Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue Euclid First Data Release

papers.t: SimpleClock: a satellite-disciplined oscillator for astronomical instrumentation
papers.abs: SimpleClock is a low-cost, high-stability timing reference designed for astronomical experiments that combines a global navigation satellite system (GNSS) timing receiver, a digitally tunable 10 MHz microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) oven-controlled oscillator, external thermal regulation and autonomous control. It provides 10 MHz and pulse-per-second references at an estimated prototype hardware cost of US\$500. Independently enabled frequency and phase feedback support precise point positioning (PPP) with Galileo's High Accuracy Service (HAS), satellite-based augmentation system (SBAS) solutions and standalone operation. Three-unit phase comparisons separate component noise and characterize disciplined-output stability over 200\,000 s recordings. Across five configurations, each analysed over 200\,000 s, equivalent single-unit differential Allan deviation and time deviation at 1000 s span $3.5\times10^{-13}$--$1.0\times10^{-12}$ and 115--447 ps, respectively. The maximum equivalent time deviation over averaging times from 1 to 50\,000 s spans 143--1090 ps. These results support applications in astronomical timing, including low-frequency very long baseline interferometry (VLBI).

papers.t: ZTF J2229+1928: A 23 Minute Eclipsing Double White Dwarf Binary
papers.abs: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Submitted to AAS Journals

papers.t: A flash before dawn: 21 cm signatures of transient reionization from supermassive Pop III stars
papers.abs: Recent data from cosmological galaxy surveys combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data give a preference for a departure from $Λ$CDM, favoring a model with an evolving dark energy equation of state or a small neutrino mass. However, recent works have shown that the electron scattering optical depth to the CMB ($τ$) can reduce this preference if $τ\sim0.09$, larger than that preferred by CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data. With standard monotonic hydrogen reionization histories, such a high value of $τ$ is in strong tension with spectroscopic galaxy data constraining the end of reionization. Thus, high-$τ$ models are restricted to non-standard reionization scenarios, where astrophysical sources inject an appreciable amount of ionizing photons at early times. One recently studied model for this is a supermassive population III star scenario, where radiative feedback from a self-annihilating dark matter particle enables a pathway to form $M\sim10^5 M_\odot$ stars that, upon collapse, photoionize a surrounding volume large enough to source appreciable contributions to $τ$ as a population. Here we present the first self-consistent treatment of the feedback from these supermassive population III stars within a large semi-numerical cosmological simulation, accounting for their ionizing, Lyman-Werner, and X-ray feedback on the intergalactic medium. We use it to predict the distinct signatures on the large-scale 21 cm signal at Cosmic Dawn, and forecast its detectability. We find that the 21 cm power spectrum probed by future radio survey arrays like the Square Kilometre Array could detect signatures of these supermassive population III at high significance and set model-dependent constraints on $τ$ that approach $σ_τ\sim0.012$, enough to distinguish our fiducial $τ\sim0.097$ scenario from current Planck values at $>3σ$.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, submitted to PRD

papers.t: Transient early reionization allows for a high optical depth while remaining consistent with kSZ measurements
papers.abs: Recent works have shown that a CMB optical depth of $τ\approx0.09$, above the Planck low-$\ell$ polarization value of 0.054, would weaken the preference of DESI data for dynamical dark energy and for a low neutrino mass. Apart from the low-$\ell$ CMB, another probe that prefers a $τ\sim0.055$ is the kinetic Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect when combined with the end of hydrogen reionization as measured by the Ly$α$ forest. In this work we use a new self-consistent model of supermassive Population~III stars, which partially ionize the intergalactic medium at high redshifts ($z\approx20$--$25$), to predict the kSZ signal. We show that such an early, transient reionization phase can raise $τ$ to $\approx0.09$ while remaining consistent with current kSZ and Ly-$α$ forest constraints. We forecast that the Simons Observatory, combined with Ly-$α$ forest and UV luminosity function data, can constrain the optical depth accumulated above $z=12$ to $\pm0.008$ in our fiducial supermassive Pop~III scenario.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures plus supplemental material

papers.t: PSR J1807-2459B in NGC 6544: A Unique Relativistic Binary in a Dense Cluster
papers.abs: The globular cluster NGC 6544 is a high-density, dynamically evolved system located in the direction of the Galactic Center, known for hosting the eccentric binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1807-2459B. We present a new timing solution for this pulsar, based on more than 26 years of observations with the Parkes, Green Bank and MeerKAT radio telescopes. We measure for the first time the variation of the orbital period, which is dominated by the acceleration of the binary in the cluster potential: this places the pulsar in front of the cluster center and reveals its intrinsic spin-down, typical of a fully recycled millisecond pulsar. We also improve the measurements of the rate of advance of periastron and of the Einstein delay, the latter by a factor of four, and include the previously neglected contributions of the proper motion, which makes these parameters and the derived masses of the pulsar and its companion, $1.3636^{+0.0017}_{-0.0021}\,M_\odot$ and $1.2071^{+0.0021}_{-0.0017}\,M_\odot$, more realistic. Together with the Shapiro delay, these measurements allow two independent tests of general relativity, both passed. Our results show that precise post-Keplerian parameters of a binary pulsar in a dense cluster can probe both the cluster gravitational field and general relativity, provided that kinematic effects are carefully taken into account.

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Photometric-redshift pipeline overview and validation
papers.abs: We present the pipeline design of the photometric redshift processing function for Data Release 1 (DR1) of the $Euclid$ mission, and the validation and performance of our cosmology-related products that are released as part of DR1-Foundation. The $Euclid$ mission aims to constrain the equation-of-state parameter of dark energy, $w$, to percent-level accuracy through the measurement of large-scale structure via weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering. As part of DR1-Foundation we release determinations of photometric redshifts (photo-$z$), corrected photometry, and object classes that are used to form the basis of the cosmological samples. The release furthermore includes estimates of the spectral energy distributions of stars and galaxies for the careful modelling of the point-spread function for weak-lensing measurement. We estimate the performance of the photo-$z$ point estimates and probability distribution functions using overlapping spectroscopic redshifts, which are weighted to match different flux-limited target samples. We find that the current performance is somewhat below mission design requirements ($40\%$ in scatter and a factor of 2 in outlier fraction) at the nominal survey depth ($I_{\rm E}<24.5$), but closely matching requirements at slightly brighter magnitudes ($I_{\rm E}<24$), consistent with pre-launch analyses and the slightly shallower external data (up to $0.3\,\mathrm{mag}$) with respect to end-of-mission expectations. Data from Rubin-LSST will help alleviate this issue by the time of the final cosmology analyses. The other cosmology-related outputs are tested to the extent that is possible with currently available comparison data. This paper is partnered by an article describing the measurement of the physical properties of galaxies for the purpose of non-cosmological science.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"

papers.t: OGLE Pre-discovery Observations of the Dwarf Planet Candidate 2026 ED138
papers.abs: The newly discovered trans-Neptunian object, 2026 ED138, is a strong dwarf planet candidate detected by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Despite its high intrinsic brightness, it evaded detection by previous sky surveys as it hid near crowded Galactic disk fields. Here, we present an analysis of precovery observations of 2026 ED138 in archival data from the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE). We identify 102 reliable detections of the object as it moved across the dense regions of the Galactic plane and bulge between 2011 and 2024. We provide precise astrometric and photometric measurements of the object. Modeling its phase curve yields absolute magnitudes of H_I = 2.224 +/- 0.034 mag and H_V = 3.154 +/- 0.035 mag. Period analysis of the phase-angle-corrected light curve reveals a candidate rotation period of 1.18077 days and its 1-day alias 0.54066 days, although a low signal-to-noise ratio renders these periodicities tentative.
papers.comment: submitted to Acta Astronomica

papers.t: The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable
papers.abs: Majorana fermions can carry neither charge nor dipole moments, leaving the anapole moment as their leading electromagnetic interaction. A stable Majorana fermion is therefore a minimal realization of electromagnetically interacting dark matter. The momentum dependence of the anapole interaction produces a harder recoil spectrum than standard momentum-independent interactions. We show that this makes elastically scattering anapole dark matter a viable interpretation of the single high-energy nuclear-recoil event recorded by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, in a region where almost no background is expected. Curiously, the same coupling that fits the LZ data also yields the observed dark matter abundance at a mass of about 300 GeV, and is consistent with collider searches and indirect detection. The scenario is testable, predicting further events at lower energies, which the full LZ run will probe and a next-generation detector such as XLZD will decisively test.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 3 figures

papers.t: Do magnetic cycles of Sun-like stars exhibit Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule?
papers.abs: One intriguing feature of the solar magnetic cycle is its alternating cycle amplitude: the even-numbered cycles are usually followed by stronger odd-numbered cycles, popularly known as the Gnevyshev-Ohl rule (or the even-odd effect). In this study, we probe whether Gnevyshev-Ohl-like trends exist in stellar cycles of Sun-like stars, utilizing the Mount Wilson Observatory (MWO) chromospheric $S$-index data as a proxy for the stellar magnetic field. We apply quasi-Planck and skewed-Gaussian function fits to extract the cycle peaks from the MWO $S$-index data and consider the stars that have a minimum of four usable cycles. First, we say that Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule is obeyed in any star for a pair of even-odd or odd-even cycles, if the second cycle in the pair is stronger. For this definition, we find that many of the stars considered, especially slow rotators, hold the Gnevyshev-Ohl-like trends quite well, with the fraction of cycles obeying the GO-rule been $1.0$ for these stars. However, we do not find any significant correlation between the fraction of cycles obeying the rule and the rotation period or the Rossby number of the star. Next, we examine Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule in the stellar cycles using alternative definitions for the rule. Saying that the rule holds as long as the middle cycle has a maximum or minimum in sets of consecutive three cycles, we obtain a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.25 $(p=0.299)$ and 0.59 (0.007), between the GO-rule fraction and the rotation period and Rossby number respectively, for the skewed-Gaussian fit data. Inspite of the fact, that our analysis suffers from a lack of sufficient number of good-quality cycles, we be believe that our results can still shed some light on the dynamo mechanism in other Sun-like stars and its dependence on rotation.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Accepted in MNRAS

papers.t: Mass Loss Rates of Evolved Stars in Isolated Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abs: We derive the mass-loss rates of asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars in the isolated dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 6822 using SEDust, an automated pipeline that fits spectral energy distributions (SEDs) to estimate stellar mass-loss and dust-production rates. The total mass-loss rate of the AGB population is $(3.7 \pm 1.1) \times 10^{-3} M_\odot\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. For a gas-to-dust ratio of 200, this corresponds to a dust injection rate of $2.0 \times 10^{-5} M_\odot\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. If sustained over 10 Gyr, this rate would yield approximately $2 \times 10^{5} M_\odot$ of dust, which is lower than the dust mass of $2.7 \times 10^{5} M_\odot$ estimated from Herschel observations. AGB stars alone therefore cannot account for the present-day dust reservoir of NGC 6822, and additional sources or processes, such as dust growth in the interstellar medium, are required.

papers.t: A Remote-Sensing Framework for Interpreting CME Transit Effects
papers.abs: We develop a remote-sensing framework to diagnose coronal mass ejection (CME) transit effects by comparing observed density evolution with an idealized self-similar reference shell and snowplow-based compression benchmarks. We apply the method to the 27 January 2012 CME using STEREO/SECCHI COR2-A and COR2-B and SOHO/LASCO C3. Electron-density profiles are extracted along the CME front in position-angle sectors and compared with synthetic profiles from a forward-modeled GCS shell. Sector-wise power-law fits quantify the radial density falloff and reveal substantial azimuthal variability. In COR2-A, several western sectors flatten relative to the synthetic shell and approach the snowplow-like compression regime, while other sectors show steeper-than-synthetic declines. COR2-B and LASCO C3 provide complementary viewpoints and also show sector-dependent departures, although the detailed pattern changes with viewing geometry. Conservative excess-density criteria identify clear pile-up only in localized COR2-A sectors, indicating that compression is spatially structured rather than uniform across the front. Comparison with snowplow benchmarks also depends strongly on the assumed upstream solar-wind conditions. These results show that CME-front density evolution is better described as a mixed system containing compression-dominated regions together with localized steepening that may reflect depletion, redistribution of material, or erosion-like evolution. The framework provides a practical way to separate competing processes that modify CME structure during heliospheric transit.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 16 figures

papers.t: Anatomy of LyC Escape in MEGATRON: Connecting Feedback Physics to Demographics, Leakage Timescales, and Explorations of ISM Density as a Tracer of Escape Fraction
papers.abs: Constraining the Lyman Continuum (LyC) escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$) of high-redshift galaxies is essential to connect the abundant populations revealed by \textit{JWST} to cosmic reionization. We investigate this interplay using {\small MEGATRON}, a suite of zoom simulations with detailed radiation/chemistry and varied feedback prescriptions. We find that feedback physics simultaneously regulates UV source counts, LyC escape fractions, and escaping ionizing luminosities ($\dot{N}_{\rm ion,esc}$), producing different reionization histories. These differences are governed by the delay between a starburst and LyC escape: efficient early feedback and lower-density environments enable photons to escape while pre-supernovae stellar populations remain strongly ionizing. Consequently, models that produce fewer UV-bright galaxies yield earlier LyC escape and reionize sooner than models with more abundant UV sources and delayed LyC emission. Furthermore, UV-faint galaxies follow a common physical sequence in ISM structure with increasing $f_{\rm esc}$ irrespective of feedback physics: stronger leakers ($1\%\leq f_{\rm esc}\leq 50\%$) exhibit evidence of strong photoionization and SNe feedback alongside post-starburst star formation histories, while extreme leakers ($f_{\rm esc}\geq 50\%$) have also cleared their cold/dense ISM. We find that electron densities inferred from the $\rm [O\,{II}]\,λ\lambda3727$ doublet are a candidate diagnostic of $f_{\rm esc}$, with lower densities around $\rm H~{\small II}$ regions selecting stronger leakers. Moreover, this density can trace the early evolution of $f_{\rm esc}$, whereas UV slope-based calibrations over-predict $\dot{N}_{\rm ion,esc}$ for individual young galaxies by up to two orders of magnitude. Overall, the delayed duty cycle of LyC leakage must be accounted for when UV source counts are interpreted in the context of reionization.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 15 figures, 3 appendices (3 figures). Comments are very welcome!

papers.t: Where Do Population~III Stars Form? Unveiling Late PopIII-Forming Environments with CampFIRE-6k
papers.abs: Population III (PopIII) stars are the first generation of metal-free stars, thought to form in minihalos ($M_\mathrm{halo} \sim10^5-10^6\,\mathrm{M_{\odot}}$) at Cosmic Dawn ($z\gtrsim15$) before largely giving way to Population II stars formed from the newly enriched medium. Simulations show, however, that PopIII stars may continue forming at low rates through the Epoch of Reionization (EoR, $z \sim 6 - 10$), due to the inhomogeneous enrichment of the Universe. Nonetheless, significant uncertainty remains on the rates and typical environments of late PopIII formation. We use the CampFIRE-6k cosmological zoom-in simulation to examine PopIII star formation history and environments through $z\sim6$. We find that PopIII stars form at a near constant rate ($\sim 10^{-3.5} ~\mathrm{M_{\odot}\,yr^{-1}\,cMpc ^{-3}}$) through $z=6$, including within atomic-cooling halos ($M_\mathrm{halo}\sim 10^7-10^8\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$) at late times.
papers.comment: 3 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to RNAAS

papers.t: Swept by the Galactic Tide: How Galactic Tides and Stellar Encounters Drive the Evolution of Wide Binaries and Their Giant Planets
papers.abs: Wide stellar binaries ($a_b > 10^3$ AU) are common throughout the Galaxy, and many host extrasolar planets. Comparing planets in wide binaries with those around single stars can reveal whether a distant stellar companion affects planet formation. Such a comparison cannot be made directly, however: unlike in single-star systems, the Galactic tide and passing field stars dramatically reshape wide binaries over Gyr timescales, influencing the orbital properties and stability of the planets they host. In this work, we present N-body simulations demonstrating how the Galactic tide and stellar encounters sculpt the orbits of super-Jupiters on 1-6.5 AU orbits in wide binary systems on Sun-like Galactic orbits over 9 Gyr. We predict systematically higher orbital eccentricities for planets in wide binaries compared to single-star systems, with the most significant differences in older systems and those with more massive binary companions. Planetary ejections and disruptions are also common, and we find that planet-hosting binaries with orbits nearly perpendicular to the Galactic midplane are preferentially depleted. In our most optimistic estimate, the maximum hot Jupiter production rate is enhanced by up to a factor of ~3 relative to binaries without Galactic perturbations. A significant fraction of these binaries are also ionized (the stars become unbound), with a preference for ionization in lower-mass binaries, while the eccentricity distribution of survivors relaxes from mildly superthermal to nearly thermal. These results provide testable predictions for the population of giant planets in wide binaries soon to be revealed by Gaia DR4 and DR5.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 19 figures. To be submitted to AAS Journals. Comments welcome!

papers.t: Sailing with the winds of HL Tau: the JWST view
papers.abs: Studying protostellar ejections is crucial to understanding the formation of young stars and planetary systems. The Class I/II star HL Tau, with its ringed disk and prominent bipolar outflows, is a benchmark system for these studies. We provide a first overview of our Cycle 3 JWST program targeting HL Tau, focusing on the morphology and kinematics of the various wind components as well as on the water emission lines excited in the inner disk. Our observations cover the 1.66-28 $μ$m spectral range, combining NIRSpec and MIRI MRS mosaics to map the inner 10" of the red-shifted lobe of the outflow and the base of the blue-shifted lobe. In the red-shifted lobe we observe a stratified wind of three nested layers: a fast, highly collimated atomic jet structured in a chain of eight knots and with radial velocities of 160 km/s; a wide-angle H$_2$ wind with velocities of 45 km/s exhibiting complex arc-like substructures; and a warm gas shell, of radial velocity of 35 km/s, visible in low-excitation transitions of CO ($ν$=1-0). This CO shell appears co-spatial with the CO (J=2-1) emission detected by ALMA with velocities from 3 to 25 km/s. In the first 1" of the blue-shifted lobe we detect a similar stratification, but the jet is faster and less collimated. The observed stratification and kinematics of the flow may support a magnetically driven disk-wind scenario in which the distinct components originate in the disk at progressively larger distances from the star. However, while the external components observed in CO have the laminar and regular appearance predicted for such winds, the knots in the inner jet and the arcs in the wind could be the manifestation of a pulsed ejection mechanism. Additionally, in MIRI spectra taken at the star position we detect a forest of water lines dominated by cold-to-warm (< 500 K) gas. Their distribution suggests an extended reservoir of sublimated ices.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 16 figures, accepted by A&A

papers.t: $uvby-β$ photoelectric photometry of FGK-type pulsating star candidates in the Kepler field: observations, stellar parameters and asteroseismic analysis
papers.abs: We present $uvby-β$ photoelectric photometry of 218 FGK-type stars brighter than $Kp = 12$ mag in the Kepler field. Interstellar reddening was estimated using the observed photometric indices, distances from Gaia DR3, and the Bayestar19 three-dimensional dust maps. The sample was classified into dwarf and giant stars, and their metallicities and effective temperatures were determined using empirical photometric calibrations. The resulting parameters were compared with those reported in previous photometric and spectroscopic studies. We also analyzed the Kepler long-cadence light curves of the sample and determined the global asteroseismic parameters, including the frequency of maximum oscillation power ($ν_{\max}$) and the large frequency separation ($Δν$), for red giants exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Finally, we performed a Bayesian isochrone-fitting analysis using PARSEC stellar evolutionary models, incorporating the photometric metallicities and effective temperatures, the asteroseismic parameters, and absolute visual magnitudes derived from Gaia DR3 data as observational constraints. This analysis provides estimates of the fundamental stellar parameters, including effective temperatures, metallicities, surface gravities, masses, and radii, together with their associated uncertainties.
papers.comment: 4 tables, 12 figures, accpted for publication in PASP

papers.t: FastBox: A lightweight Python package for rapid cosmological 21cm intensity mapping simulations
papers.abs: FastBox is a Python package for generating fast, physically realistic simulations of cosmological signals in three-dimensional co-moving boxes, with the primary focus of its application being 21cm intensity mapping (IM) experiments. It provides a framework for producing cosmology-dependent Gaussian and log-normal density fields, as well as modelling the effects of redshift-space distortions and linear biasing, among others. Models of instrumental systematics are incorporated, including radiometer noise and beam convolutions. Diffuse and point source foreground models are included, along with a number of foreground filtering strategies such as PCA, ICA, and transfer function correction via mock signal injection. Lastly, estimators are provided for power spectra, the two-point correlation function, and the equilateral bispectrum. The same underlying density field can also be Poisson-sampled into a discrete galaxy catalogue, so that 21cm and galaxy tracers are simulated from common initial conditions and their cross-power spectrum can be measured. Simulation grids may be cubic or anisotropic, with independent side lengths and cell counts along each Cartesian axis. FastBox is designed as a lightweight but realistic test-bench for the development and validation of end-to-end cosmological analysis pipelines.
papers.comment: Prepared for submission to JOSS

papers.t: An analytic diffusion model for viewing-angle effects in explosive transients
papers.abs: The tight observed relation between the peak bolometric luminosity, $L_{\mathrm p}$, and the width ratio $L_{30}/L_{\mathrm p}$ of Type Ia supernovae, with $L_{30}$ the luminosity 30 d after explosion, makes viewing-angle effects a useful test of explosion models. We develop an analytic diffusion model for homologously expanding asymmetric ejecta with uniform density and grey opacity, based on a Green's-function solution and an Eddington surface-emission prescription, and obtain angle-dependent light curves for a displaced spherical source and for oblate ejecta. We validate them against Monte Carlo (MC) radiative transfer and derive geometric approximations to the peak-luminosity anisotropy. For a displaced spherical source, the quasi-steady approximation, equivalent to stationary diffusion in frozen ejecta, gives $L_{\mathrm p}(θ)/L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}\simeq1+(17/8)z_{\mathrm{off}}\cosθ$, where $z_{\mathrm{off}}$ is the displacement in units of the ejecta radius, $θ$ the viewing angle from the displacement axis, and $L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}$ the angle-averaged peak. This dipole is $\mathord{\approx}10$ per cent below the finite-time value in the tested configurations. For oblate ejecta, the leading term is quadrupolar and is set by a single shape parameter. Effective models of 19 off-centre sub-Chandrasekhar explosions recover the MC peak times, peak luminosities, and width ratios to median errors of 3, 4, and 6 per cent, and the extent in $L_{\mathrm p}$ of the MC tracks, but underestimate the width-ratio variation with viewing angle by a factor of 2 to 3. An oblate construction captures the scale of peak luminosity variations in six equal-mass white-dwarf collisions. The model tracks remain inconsistent with the observed distribution, and for asymmetric models the transverse viewing-angle variation adds to the tension.

papers.t: Elemental Abundance Trends with Condensation Temperature are Unrelated to Planet Formation
papers.abs: It has been suggested that the photosphere of the Sun is depleted in the abundances of the refractory elements relative to the photospheres of nearby solar twin stars and that the degree of depletion depends on condensation temperature $T_{\text{c}}$. While the formation of the solar system's terrestrial and/or giant planets may play some role in the refractory depletion of the solar photosphere, it has also been shown that other processes can produce similar results. If the terrestrial and/or giant planet formation explanations are correct, then the depletion of refractory elemental abundances in the photospheres of terrestrial/giant exoplanet host stars should be more pronounced and therefore observable even without achieving the highest possible elemental abundance inference precisions in systems with host star surface convective zones less massive than the Sun's. For stars that host Kepler-discovered systems of terrestrial exoplanets and have low-mass surface convective zones, we do not observe the dependence of depletion on $T_{\text{c}}$ predicted by the terrestrial planet formation scenario. For a sample of stars that has been uniformly searched with the Doppler technique for giant exoplanets, we likewise show that giant exoplanet host stars are not depleted but enhanced by about $0.0063\pm 0.0004$ dex in refractory abundances compared to stars of similar masses and metallicities without giant exoplanets. Since gaps opened in protoplanetary disks by giant planets are thought to produce photospheric refractory depletion in their host stars, our observations imply that at constant metallicity giant planets are more likely to form in disks with high refractory abundances.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables. Accepted by ApJ

papers.t: A Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Andromeda: Comprehensive, All-Encompassing Spectroscopy, Imaging, and Mid-Infrared Mapping of the Nearest Giant Spiral
papers.abs: We propose a Multi-Cycle Treasury program of $\sim$800 hours that would survey Andromeda the way the Milky Way has been surveyed by APOGEE, Gaia, and WISE. - NIRSpec: spectra of $\sim$4,500 red giants and supergiants at S/N~80, sufficient for 16 elements at $\lesssim$0.05 dex precision and radial velocities to a few km s$^{-1}$. - NIRCam: $\sim$1,600 arcmin$^{2}$ in up to ten filters, reaching $\sim$20 million stars, every field imaged twice a year apart: two-epoch infrared photometry of the $\sim$500 Cepheids and $\sim$10$^{4}$ Miras in the footprint. - MIRI: $\sim$450 arcmin$^{2}$ in five filters at the depth of PHANGS. The observations are predominantly organized as twelve "bricks", each of three adjacent fields including two NIRSpec/MOS pointings, in which one instrument is prime and a second observes in parallel, so that roughly 40% of the exposure time comes at no charge. The bricks sample the nucleus, bulge, major axis to 29 kpc, minor axis, and inter-arm disk. In addition, a 100-hour grid of short NIRCam pointings with MIRI in parallel covers the HST-PHAT footprint. The result would be the first chemodynamical, star-formation, and dust map of an $L^{\star}$ galaxy other than our own built from individual stars, at a scale no single-cycle program can reach.
papers.comment: A White Paper submission on Multi-Cycle Treasury Program Concepts with JWST, comments welcome

papers.t: New line-driven mass-loss rate predictions for central stars of planetary nebulae: Luminosity dependence when approaching the Eddington limit
papers.abs: After expelling most of their envelopes, asymptotic giant branch stars turn bluewards in the Hertzsprung-Russel diagram and become hot objects. These objects ionise the surrounding material, possibly creating a planetary nebula. Because they are hot and rather luminous, they are able to launch a line-driven wind. The luminosity dependence of these winds has not yet been studied in detail using global wind models that consistently consider the interaction of the photosphere and the wind. We provide line-driven wind models of the central stars of planetary nebulae focusing on the dependence of these winds on luminosity. While the mass-loss rate is strongly sensitive to stellar luminosity, the terminal velocity increases with effective temperature and only weakly depends on luminosity. The predicted values agree reasonably well with observations, except that observational mass-loss rates show a rather large scatter, and the predicted terminal velocities are slightly lower than observational values. We provide ionising fluxes and show that for stars cooler than approximately 40 kK, the ionising fluxes computed from plane-parallel models are inadequate. The wind efficiency stays rather weak, which implies that the Wolf-Rayet type of central stars is connected with objects with an elevated mass fraction of heavy elements.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NISP spectroscopy of gravitational arcs and multiple images
papers.abs: Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release". 15 pages, 5 figures

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): VIS processing and data products
papers.abs: This paper describes the characteristics of the Euclid visible imager (VIS) data delivered as part of the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). This data set contains 42092 calibrated frames. Validated nominal exposures cover 2092 deg$^2$ of sky. We outline the minor changes made to the VIS processing function (PF) since previous releases. For the wide survey, the photometric and astrometric accuracy of the reference stellar sample $(18.5 < I_{\rm E} < 19.8)$ is excellent. The internal and external astrometric dispersions are 0.08 and 0.18 mas, respectively, at the quadrant level, and 3.4 and 5.6 mas at the source level. The corresponding internal and external photometric dispersions are 0.76 and 1.4 mmag at the quadrant level, and 11 and 25 mmag at the source level. We characterise remaining astrometric and photometric systematic effects: focal-plane-dependent variations; time-dependent photometric offsets; and colour-dependent centroid shifts. The noise floor in the deepest VIS images appears to be set by the extended diffuse light of faint galaxies. Globally, the DR1 VIS data meet pre-launch mission requirements and the 42092 images it contains provide our first substantial look at the sky as seen by VIS.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) C: Lens modelling pipeline overview
papers.abs: Galaxy-scale strong lenses provide precise measurements of galaxy mass distributions, magnified views of distant galaxies, and a competitive cosmological probe. Historically, such studies have been limited to hundreds of lenses, with automated modelling methods proving difficult to scale. We present automated lens modelling of 15 072 strong-lens candidates from Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), over an order of magnitude larger than any previously modelled sample. Using PyAutoLens-JAX, we perform three fits with multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE), pixelised, and Sérsic representations of the source, adopting an isothermal ellipsoid mass model with external shear. These fits provide foreground lens-light subtraction, adaptive Delaunay source reconstructions, and deblended photometry. More than 20 expert inspectors visually assess the resulting models, and each model is assigned the classification on which at least 75% of its inspectors agree. Of the 6073 grade A (secure) lens candidates, inspectors classify 4098 (67.5%) as successfully modelled, 580 (9.6%) as failures, 317 (5.2%) as multi-galaxy lenses, 15 (0.2%) as double-source-plane lenses, and 7 (0.1%) as unsure if lens, while 1032 (17.0%) reach no consensus and 24 (0.4%) have incomplete models. For the 8999 grade B (probable) candidates, the modelling success rate falls to 43.1%, primarily reflecting an increase in cases without consensus (37.6%), rather than a comparable increase in agreed failures (12.9%). Successfully modelled grade A and B systems have a median effective Einstein radius of 0.85 arcsec and a median total $I_E$-band source magnification of 8.1. We publicly release the successful lens models, their inferred properties, and magnified-source reconstructions through the ECLIPSE catalogue, demonstrating automated modelling at Euclid sample sizes and enabling population-level strong-lensing science.
papers.comment: 29 pages, 16 figures. Submitted to A&A. Catalogue: https://euclid-eclipse-lenses.org; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19654904

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
papers.abs: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, submitted to A&A. Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
papers.abs: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.
papers.comment: 28 pages. Submitted to A&A as part of the Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"

papers.t: A statistical study of ionized outflows in low-mass galaxies from DESI DR1
papers.abs: We present a statistical analysis of ionized gas outflows in a large sample of low-mass ($\mathrm{log(M_{*}/M_{\odot})\lesssim10}$) galaxies at $z<0.45$ from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). Using [OIII] and H$α$ emission lines, we identify $\sim5800$ dwarf galaxies with robust signatures of ionized outflows. Most are star-forming systems above the star-forming main sequence, with a smaller fraction of composites and AGN hosts. The derived mass-loading factors span $η=0.001-1$, with a median $η\sim0.01$, consistent with previous studies at similar stellar masses. These values are $1$--$2$ dex lower than predicted by cosmological simulations, suggesting that the ionized phase traces only a minor fraction of the total outflow mass. Outflow velocities are sufficient to enrich the circumgalactic medium in $\gtrsim80\%$ of cases, while escape into the intergalactic medium appears efficient mainly in composite and AGN hosts. We find that mass-loading factors decrease with stellar mass, broadly reproducing simulated trends despite the normalization offset. Comparing individual detections with stacked spectra of the general low-mass star-forming population, we find systematically lower mass-loading factors in the stacks, although the difference decreases toward larger offsets above the star-forming main sequence. Together with a positive correlation between mass-loading factor and specific star-formation rate, this suggests that enhanced star formation and burstiness regulate feedback efficiency and shape galactic winds. Our results highlight the role of ionized outflows in the baryon cycle of low-mass galaxies and the need for multiphase studies to fully understand feedback in galaxy evolution.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: Measuring the growth index in the $w_0w_a$CDM background
papers.abs: We produce a measurement of the growth index, $γ$, which is used to parametrize the scale-independent growth of linear matter perturbations on sub-horizon scales, for the $w_0w_a$CDM background model. In 2023, assuming the $Λ$CDM background, the value $γ=0.633^{+0.025}_{-0.024}$ was obtained, excluding the General Relativity value of $γ=0.55$ at $3.7σ$ statistical significance. In 2025, an analysis of baryon acoustic oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopy Instrument (DESI) demonstrated a preference for a dynamical dark energy over the cosmological constant model, $Λ$, ranging from $2.8-4.2σ$, depending on the external datasets used. Therefore it is important to determine how the $γ$ measurement is modified in the context of dynamical dark energy and verify whether the tension with the expected theoretical value persists. Considering data from Planck cosmic microwave background anisotropies, $fσ_{8}$, baryon acoustic oscillation from DESI and supernova Ia luminosity distances from Phanteon+, we find $γ_{w_0w_a}=0.633\pm0.024$, essentially the same value found for the $Λ$CDM background. This result excludes the General Relativity value for the $w_0w_a$CDM background evolution at $3.4σ$ level. We also show that the $γ$ posteriors across many datasets combinations are consistent with each other and that main driver of the "$γ$ tension" is the $fσ_{8}$ dataset.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures

papers.t: Automated identification of dipole mixed-modes in red-giant stars
papers.abs: Dipole mixed modes probe the internal structure of red giants by carrying information from both the convective envelope and the radiative core. Hence, identifying these modes allows for the determination of evolutionary states and stellar interior conditions. This identification typically relies on comparing observed frequencies with theoretical ones derived from the mixed-mode asymptotic relation. However, the process is challenging due to parameter-space degeneracies, stellar rotation, as well as missing modes and spurious peaks in the power density spectrum. In this work, we aim to develop an automated method for identifying dipole mixed modes, suitable for large-scale asteroseismic analyses. We introduce a metric that measures the overlap between observed and asymptotic dipole frequencies, represented as spike trains convolved with Gaussian kernels. After optimising this metric with a genetic algorithm, we use the best-fit parameters to perform a global assignment of the oscillation modes. We then validated the method using synthetic frequencies of RGB and CHeB stars perturbed by stellar rotation, and further tested it on four benchmark stars. Validation using perturbed synthetic frequencies shows that our method recovers over 95% of the dipole mixed modes across different evolutionary states, and this performance remains robust to spurious peaks and missing modes. For the benchmark stars, our dipole mode identification is consistent with previously published results, with mixed-mode parameter estimates typically agreeing within 1% for $ΔΠ$1 and 10% for $δν$rot and $q$. Our analysis demonstrates that the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges associated with the complex dipole mode spectrum. Thus, it enables automated identification of dipole mixed modes, supporting homogeneous, large-scale asteroseismic analyses of evolved stars.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 13 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A. Abstract abridged for arXiv submission

papers.t: Identification of extragalactic radio sources in the VISTA survey of the Magellanic Clouds using an unsupervised machine learning algorithm
papers.abs: The Magellanic Clouds benefit from a wealth of data across the electromagnetic spectrum, but extracting extragalactic sources from these crowded fields is a less than straightforward endeavour. We used an unsupervised machine learning algorithm (t-distributed stochastic neighbourhood embedding; t-SNE) to classify 6,652 and 1,356 sources in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, respectively, that were detected in the VISTA Survey of the Magellanic Clouds (VMC) and the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). Multi-wavelength photometry and colours from optical to radio were used as features to cluster similar sources together in 2D space on a t-SNE map. We used previously classified sources to separate the clusters into five classes: AGN, low-redshift galaxies, blazars, dusty stellar objects (e.g. young stellar objects, planetary nebulæ etc) and high proper-motion stars. Previous photometric classifications from the literature match with specific clusters identified, as well as provide insight on areas of the t-SNE map for which there are no previous classifications. This work shows that the combination of unsupervised machine learning with photometry from optical to radio has proven adept at separating the stellar from the extragalactic, and the AGN from the galaxies. Our associated new spectroscopy with SALT includes new discoveries of AGN up to redshift 3.3 and Magellanic emission-line objects.
papers.comment: MNRAS accepted

papers.t: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
papers.abs: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 πf(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to ApJ

papers.t: Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks
papers.abs: Quantum sensor networks can use the spatial phase coherence of wavelike dark matter to probe not only particle properties but also the motion and structure of the Galactic halo. We explore this idea for the minimal two-node network, in which a nonlocal exchange measurement samples the characteristic function of the velocity distribution. We compare the Standard Halo Model (SHM) with a Gaia-inspired radially anisotropic component and their mixture (SHM++), taking into account daily and annual modulation, postselection, depolarizing events, and a flat instrumental offset. We show that annual modulation at one fixed local sidereal time has the same phase waveform for the centered SHM and Gaia-inspired SHM++ models, leaving them degenerate when the overall signal amplitude is unknown. Earth's rotation breaks this degeneracy by scanning the baseline through Galactic directions and exposing the direction-dependent coherence of an anisotropic population. Distinguishing these velocity distributions would test whether the local halo is smooth and nearly isotropic or contains a radially biased accreted component, turning a quantum-network detection into a probe of Milky Way structure. Our likelihood analysis shows how modulation and signal-odd controls separate this information from flat backgrounds and provides a path from model discrimination toward measurement of the local velocity distribution.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 6 figures, 1 table

papers.t: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) D: Photometric redshifts and the first census of strong lenses in the galaxy evolution framework
papers.abs: The Euclid mission is revolutionising the study of strong gravitational lenses by providing high-resolution imaging over an unprecedented survey area, increasing the number of known lenses by two orders of magnitude compared to previous surveys. Characterising this sample of lens-galaxies requires accurate measurements of their physical properties. However, standard catalogue photometry often blends the light from the foreground lens and the lensed background source, limiting the reliability of derived galaxy parameters. We present a homogeneous catalogue of photometric redshifts and physical properties for 9538 galaxy-scale strong lenses identified in Euclid's DR1 strong-lens sample. We use deblended multiwavelength photometry obtained from the lens modelling of Euclid and ground-based images with PyAutoLens. The photometric redshifts of the lens galaxies are estimated using the template-fitting code Phosphoros. The stellar masses, SFRs, stellar ages, and metallicities are inferred through SED fitting with Prospector, adopting a flexible non-parametric SFH and a Salpeter IMF. The robustness of the inferred parameters is assessed through comparisons with spectroscopic redshifts and external galaxy surveys. The sample of lenses spans a broad redshift range of $0.13\lesssim z_{\rm phot} \lesssim 1.98$, with a median $z_{\rm phot} = 0.68^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$. The sample is dominated by massive quiescent galaxies with a $M_\ast$ range $[10^{10},\,10^{12.1}]\,M_\odot$ and a median $\log_{10}(M_\ast/M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$. This catalogue represents one of the first large-scale characterisations of strong-lens galaxies in the Euclid era. By combining deblended photometry with homogeneous photometric redshift and SED-fitting analyses, it provides a foundation for studies of galaxy evolution, lens-galaxy scaling relations, and the connection between stellar and total mass in strong lenses.
papers.comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''

papers.t: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.abs: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 11 figures

papers.t: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.abs: We present the discovery of new secondary delayed radio flares from two tidal disruption events (TDEs), AT2019ehz and AT2019eve from observations ranging 1-18 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. For AT2019ehz, we find a secondary flare in radio emission began at 1545 days post-disruption, 770 days after the first radio flare detected at 775 days post-disruption, and for AT2019eve the secondary flare was detected at 1594 days post-disruption, 825 days after its initial radio detection at 769 days post-disruption. Through spectral modeling of the multi-frequency observations, we extract physical parameters of the new flares to constrain the origin of the rebrightening. We find the secondary flare of AT2019ehz is likely produced by a second outflow launched at roughly 1000 days. For AT2019eve, the secondary flare reveals unexpected spectral evolution with a self-absorbed peak increasing from 1325 to 2173 days post-disruption, which is not well explained with most models of expanding outflows and instead suggests a more complex physical geometry. This inconclusive origin of AT2019eve highlights the need for more complex models to explain observed TDE radio evolution.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 8 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.t: Dual-species atom interferometry for axion dark matter
papers.abs: Atom interferometers are sensitive to oscillations of the masses and transition frequencies of atoms, which can be induced by axion dark matter. The main limitation is the sensitivity to gravity gradient noise (GGN). We propose a dual-species atom interferometry sequence that provides a suppression of GGN by up to three orders of magnitude and a sensitivity enhancement via the mass difference of the two atoms. We show that, under realistic experimental assumptions, a 10m-baseline dual-species atom interferometer is more sensitive to the axion gluon coupling than a 100m single-species gradiometer. Including a comprehensive noise analysis, we demonstrate that the Very Long Baseline Atom Interferometer (VLBAI) in Hannover with a baseline of 10m can probe the axion decay constant at levels almost competitive with leading laboratory constraints. The proposed 100m-baseline Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE) can extend this sensitivity by up to two orders of magnitude, surpassing laboratory constraints for axion masses of $10^{-19}\;\text{eV}/c^2 \lesssim m_a \lesssim 3\times10^{-15}\;\text{eV}/c^2$.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures

papers.t: Toward the minimal set of states in axion superradiance
papers.abs: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.
papers.comment: 37 pages, 25 figures. Code and data available at Github/Zenodo

papers.t: oMEGACat. XI. Kinematic Characterization of Omega Centauri's Subpopulations: A Flattened Primordial Component
papers.abs: Omega Centauri ($ω$ Cen; NGC 5139), the likely stripped nucleus of a dwarf galaxy accreted by the Milky Way, is one of the few galactic nuclei resolvable into individual stars. Because of its long relaxation time, the kinematics of its stars may still retain memory of how this nucleus formed. We combine HST proper motions and MUSE line-of-sight velocities from the oMEGACat survey to compare populations defined by abundance variations (the chromosome map), metallicity, and age within the half-light radius. The chromosome-map division separates two dynamically distinct components. The primordial stars have a flattened dispersion field, with kinematic ellipticity $ε\approx 0.7$ ($σ_{\rm minor} / σ_{\rm major} \approx 0.8$), which we recover independently in the line-of-sight velocities and the proper motions. The enriched stars are consistent with $ε=0$ in the line-of-sight velocities and are no more flattened than the full sample in the proper motions, and the two components show no strong difference in rotation. Metallicity bins show no comparable structure, because each bin mixes stars from both components, and the age-metallicity sample covers only the cluster core, where it cannot test for the flattening. The present-day central concentration of the most enriched (P2) stars suggests that they formed more centrally concentrated than the primordial stars, independent of assembly scenario. These results favor a picture in which the primordial stars retain the flattened orbital structure of the progenitor, while the enriched stars fell inward as dense clumps or formed in compact, centrally concentrated starbursts.
papers.comment: 29 pages, 19 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJ. Comments welcome

papers.t: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
papers.abs: Frequency-dependent radio time delays have been measured in Sgr A* light curves, with higher-frequency emission generally leading lower-frequency emission. These lags have been interpreted in terms of an organized jet-like outflow, expanding plasma components, or magnetic-flux eruptions, although their origin and recurrence remain uncertain. We aim to search for and quantify frequency-dependent radio time delays in a new high-cadence Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observation of Sgr A*. Using the improved broad 12-37 GHz frequency coverage, we measured the timing of the dominant variability feature and compared the resulting lag-wavelength slope with previous measurements. Sgr A* was observed with the VLA on 28 May 2022 in the Ku, K, and Ka bands over a 6-hour track. We extracted both band-averaged and 2 GHz subband light curves and measured the delays using a peak-time method and a locally normalized cross-correlation function. The light curves show one broad variability feature, with the maximum occurring progressively later at lower observing frequencies. Both timing methods recover a positive lag-wavelength relation, with a slope of order 40 min/cm. This value agrees with time lag results reported over more than 15 years from the first VLA observations at 22-43 GHz to later multifrequency VLA and ALMA campaigns. The sign and magnitude of the estimated delay are consistent with outward propagation through an optically thick synchrotron-emitting region. The recurrence of comparable delays over almost two decades suggests that frequency-dependent radio lags are a persistent feature of Sgr A* variability. Broadband, multi-epoch VLA monitoring of Sgr A* provides a useful probe of its radio variability, but robust lag measurements require high cadence and improved (u,v) coverage of both Sgr A* and the surrounding extended emission such as by combining different VLA configurations.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures

papers.t: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
papers.abs: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.
papers.comment: 15 pages,5 figures

papers.t: The Dark Side of the Periodic Table: Theory and Signatures of Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
papers.abs: We study the theory and signatures of a Mirror Twin Higgs (MTH) scenario in which stable twin neutrons constitute most of the dark matter (DM), while a subdominant component of twin elements survives as nuclear atomic dark matter (naDM). This framework offers a solution to the $matter~coincidence~problem$ ($Ω_{\rm DM}\simeq5Ω_b$), as the twin $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry can correlate the visible and DM mass scales and their number densities. We analyze twin nucleon freeze-out and the onset of twin Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) to estimate the total naDM abundance, and determine which elements in the dark periodic table could be populated. An appreciable but subdominant naDM component generally requires a fractional nucleon mass splitting near the percent level, with twin-BBN creating heavy elements up to twin carbon. Strong twin neutron-proton scattering allows nearly all of the dark matter, not only the atomic sub-component, to participate in $dark~acoustic~oscillations$ (DAO) at early times, giving rise to a characteristic two-stage DAO signature that may be detected with future cosmological probes. Interactions between the twin and visible sectors, including the irreducible Higgs portal, make this scenario a well-motivated target for future directional direct-detection searches, and the naDM sub-component is expected to exhibit highly exotic astrophysics. We outline a supersymmetric twin Froggatt-Nielsen realization in which spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ breaking in the flavon sector can generate the required fermion spectrum and Higgs potential.
papers.comment: 83 + 16 pages + Refs., 19 Figures, 4+2 Tables

papers.t: Cosmic Ray Heating of the Early IGM: Realistic Galaxy Populations, Reduced Efficiency, and 21-cm Signatures
papers.abs: Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.
papers.comment: 33 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to JCAP

papers.t: Dynamical evolution of the stellar mass function in multiple-population globular clusters
papers.abs: The dynamical evolution of globular clusters is significantly influenced by the multiscale structure introduced by the presence of multiple stellar populations. In this study, we investigate the long-term dynamical evolution of the stellar mass function (MF) within globular clusters hosting two stellar populations using a suite of Monte Carlo simulations run with the MOCCA code. Dynamical processes including two-body relaxation, mass segregation, and tidal stripping result in distinct radial profiles describing the variation with distance from the cluster's center of the stellar MF slope within the first population (P1), the second population (P2), and the cluster as a whole. We show that these radial profiles are well described by a broken power law with a knee located slightly interior to the half-mass radius, a feature partially driven by the multiscale structure of the multiple populations. In both 3D and 2D projected coordinates, we explore several characteristic clustercentric distances within the profile, including those where the local MF slope matches the global value of the present-day MF slope and the initial mass function (IMF) slope, and we examine how these positions evolve with the cluster's dynamical age. Our results highlight how the initially more centrally concentrated P2 drives a steeper radial gradient and a steeper MF slope in the outer regions, which subsequently affects the global cluster values. Motivated by recent observational studies suggesting that a bottom-light IMF may better describe massive globular clusters, as well as measurements of a flatter P2 MF slope in the outer regions of 47 Tucanae, we additionally explore a three-parameter bottom-light IMF and a simulation in which the P1 IMF differs from the P2 IMF, with the P2 IMF flatter than that of the P1 in the lower mass range.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 18 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
