papers.t: Exploring a Correlation Between AGN Black Hole Mass and X-ray Luminosity
papers.abs: The traditional method to measure Type-1 Active Galactic Nuclei central black hole masses ($M_{BH}$) is the reverberation mapping (RM) technique. Motivated by the desire to find a less observationally expensive method (than RM) to estimate $M_{BH}$, we have explored a purported correlation between X-ray luminosity and $M_{BH}$. For this we have compiled a sample of 35 AGN with RM $M_{BH}$ estimates that were detected in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey public data release. Using a sample that is larger than that of J. A. Mayers et al. 2018 and has a cleaner selection function, we confirm their XMM-Newton based result of a positive correlation. However, the scatter on the scaling relation remains too high ($σ_\mathrm{int}=0.50^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$) to make this a practical method to predict $M_{BH}$ for a given X-ray detected Type-1 AGN. That said, our findings can be used to improve mock X-ray skies generated from large volume hydrodynamical cosmological simulations. Such mocks are a necessary ingredient for cluster cosmology and preparation for future missions such as NewAthena.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure

papers.t: Improved constraints on axion inflation with the new code AxioGen: an efficient generator of curvature perturbations
papers.abs: Axion inflation, in which a pseudoscalar inflaton couples to a $U(1)$ gauge field via a Chern-Simons interaction, has garnered significant interest due to its rich phenomenology. The power spectrum and bispectrum for this model are often parametrized by functions known as $f_2$ and $f_3$, respectively. Previous work computed $f_2$ and $f_3$ using an approximation for the gauge field mode functions. While these approximate solutions are fairly accurate ($\mathcal{O}(10\%)$) for large values of the model parameter $ξ$, which controls gauge field particle production, our recent work has shown them to be quite inaccurate for smaller values of $ξ$. We present new fitting functions for $f_2$ and $f_3$ that are significantly more accurate than those previously used. We use these functions to place new constraints on $ξ$ and also set lower bounds for the energy scale of the axion gauge field coupling for $φ^{1/3}$ and $φ^{2/3}$ inflationary potentials. Additionally, we present a new public code to efficiently generate realizations of the primordial curvature perturbation for axion inflation in the weak backreaction regime. This code enables numerical computation of higher order correlators and provides a novel path to initial conditions for large-scale structure formation.

papers.t: Improved delensing of CMB $B$-modes with upcoming SO and LSST Year-1 mock dataset: Impact of photometric redshift errors
papers.abs: In the era of high-precision Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropy measurements, detection of primordial gravitational waves (PGWs) is one of the main goals of current CMB experiments. Detection of a divergence-free ($B$-mode) component in CMB polarisation will provide direct evidence of inflationary PGWs in the early universe. However, weak gravitational lensing of CMB photons due to intervening mass distribution of the Universe distorts the primordial polarisation patterns, introducing an additional lensing-induced $B$-mode signal. Removing these lensing-induced $B$-modes is essential for improving constraints on the amplitude of PGWs. In this work, we present a multi-tracer delensing analysis using simulations of the Rubin Observatory LSST galaxy catalogue and Simons Observatory (SO) CMB maps. We use realistic photometric redshift errors for LSST mock catalogue and high complexity Galactic foregrounds for CMB simulations. By adopting a tomographic multi-tracer approach that combines the CMB and LSST mock data, we achieved a 10-20% higher delensing efficiency compared with using CMB data alone. Our analysis removes approximately 60% of the lensing-induced $B$-mode power. We find that photometric redshift errors in the mock galaxy catalogue introduce biases in the inferred galaxy bias and $σ_{8,0}$ parameters. However, these uncertainties do not produce a significant systematic bias in the inferred tensor-to-scalar ratio.
papers.comment: under review in A&A journal

papers.t: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.abs: We searched DEAP-3600 data for neutrino signals coincident with gravitational waves from compact object mergers observed by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA collaborations (LVK). While mergers involving neutron stars are expected to produce neutrinos, these have never been detected. The DEAP-3600 experiment is sensitive to electron neutrinos as recently observed through charged current neutrino absorption on its $^{40}$Ar target. Between 2016 and 2020, the detector recorded data during seven compact merger events involving neutron stars that were observed gravitationally by LVK. Upon examination, there is no statistically significant evidence of neutrinos from any of the mergers analyzed. Exclusion limits are set on the electron neutrino fluence, e.g. from GW170817 in the mono-energetic model at $6.8\times10^{12}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$ ($1.8\times10^{10}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$) for 10 MeV (100 MeV) neutrinos.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 10 figures

papers.t: The Role of Precursors and MHD Instabilities in Distinguishing Confined and Eruptive Solar Flares
papers.abs: Identifying pre-flare magnetic conditions that determine whether a flare will be eruptive (associated with a coronal mass ejection) or confined remains a major challenge in solar physics. Motivated by previous statistical results showing that some eruptive flares occur under ideal MHD-stable conditions, we investigate the roles of kink instability (KI), torus instability (TI), preflare reconnection traced by precursor brightenings (PBs) and magnetic nonpotentiality in solar eruptiveness using an expanded sample of 68 flares above GOES class M4 from 2011--2024. To characterize the nonpotentiality of each active region (AR), we calculate the relative helicity $H_R$, current-carrying helicity $H_J$ and free magnetic energy. We find that, (1) 17 of 18 TI-unstable events and 12 of 19 KI-unstable events are eruptive, indicating that the TI parameter outperforms the KI parameter (2) although PBs are more commonly found in the MHD-unstable regime, only 3 of the 12 eruptive events in the TI/KI-stable regime show PBs, suggesting that preflare reconnection may play a secondary role compared with other factors. (3) The strongest indicator of eruptiveness is obtained by combining the TI parameter with magnetic nonpotentiality. Specifically, 24 of 36 eruptive flares satisfy $\sqrt{\left| H_J \right|}/φ\geq 0.1$ or $n \geq 1.13$, whereas 24 of 25 confined flares satisfy $\sqrt{\left| H_J \right|}/φ\le 0.1$ and $n \le 1.13$, where $φ$ is the total unsigned magnetic flux and $n$ is the decay index. These results suggest that the overall magnetic environment of ARs may play a significant role in determining the eruptiveness, in addition to the effect of MHD instability and reconnection.
papers.comment: 10 pages, two tables, accepted by ApJ

papers.t: Subpicosecond Optical Time Transfer under Simulated Motion with Electro-Optic Frequency Combs
papers.abs: Extension of high performance optical frequency comb-based time transfer to real-world systems is challenged by platform motion, particularly for large relative velocities. Here, we utilize agile electro-optic frequency combs to construct a laboratory-based simulator of a two-way optical time transfer system under motion. Through direct control of the electro-optic frequency comb parameters, we can artificially induce the effects of relative motion. We performed tests of the time transfer performance across a km-scale fiber link for velocity profiles that linearly increase from rest up to 400 m/s. Through a post-processed data analysis, we demonstrate continuous tracking of the clock offset between sites with subpicosecond precision throughout the velocity sweep. These results illustrate the versatility of using electro-optic frequency combs for optical time transfer in deployed systems.

papers.t: CCGeant4: charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions in Geant4
papers.abs: CCGeant4 models energy-loss fluctuations of heavy ions in Geant4, accounting for both charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation. We use GLOBAL cross sections for electron capture and loss, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers and charge-dependent delta-electron spectra calculated from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential. The package also supports tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering. The silicon example includes interference between Coulomb and nuclear scattering amplitudes. We compare charge evolution with GLOBAL and energy-loss spectra with MOCADI for matched beams and targets. Experimental comparisons cover the energy-loss measurements of Weick et al. and several measurements of energy deposited by xenon ions in silicon. For uranium at 800 MeV/u, the energy-loss variances from our Dirac configuration agree with the screened-ion calculations of Weick et al. to within 4% in Be, Al and Pb. Both calculations lie within the reported experimental uncertainties for all three targets, while calculated bismuth spectra in silver are narrower than measured. Calculations in thin silicon layers show that delta-electron escape can make deposited-energy distributions substantially narrower than primary-ion energy-loss distributions, highlighting the importance of secondary-electron transport for detector-response modelling. The distribution includes the Geant4 source patch, the transport tables and their converters, and a runnable example.

papers.t: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: Brown Dwarfs in the Blanco 1 Open Cluster
papers.abs: A 35.6\,deg$^2$ field of Euclid Data Release~1 that covers part of the corona and tidal tails of the young (100--130\,Myr) nearby (234\,pc) open cluster Blanco~1 is presented. We select 22 ultracool dwarfs from Euclid photometry and slitless spectra, and measure proper motions over a median baseline of 13\,yr by combining Euclid astrometry with VIKING, KiDS and Rubin positions. Ten objects are comoving late-M and L dwarf candidates with membership probabilities of at least 0.5 under two field models. Nine of them are typed from their Euclid spectra, and the tenth is a candidate only if its colour-based type is adopted. Brown dwarf evolutionary models give masses of 0.03--0.06\,$M_\odot$ for the cluster age. The substellar population is about twice that predicted by a lognormal mass function scaled to the cluster's Gaia members. The remaining 12 objects are classified as late-M, L and T dwarfs with low probability of membership in the cluster. Using the Euclid sample to calibrate a search over 246\,deg$^2$ of VIKING and KiDS photometry and motions, we identify 60 ultracool candidates, with about seven expected by chance. In the core region of Blanco 1 archival Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam images and motions over 2011--2025 yield 35 candidates of types M7 or later, at least 20 of which are kinematic members at 95\% confidence. These results extend the spectroscopic sequence of Blanco 1 into the L-type brown dwarfs and the list of candidate members over the outskirts and tidal tails of the cluster.
papers.comment: 59 pages, 23 figures, submitted to The Astrophysical Journal

papers.t: Population inference of eccentric binary black holes using asymptotic constants of motion
papers.abs: In standard gravitational-wave population analyses of compact binaries, source parameters are defined at a reference frequency. For quantities that evolve during the inspiral, this means constructing a population of systems at different evolutionary stages, which complicates the astrophysical interpretation of the results. The past-time infinity, or zero-frequency, limit provides a mathematically well-defined reference where all sources enter the population fit on equal footing. This approach was first proposed for spin tilts, which evolve due to spin precession but converge to constant values as binaries are back-propagated. The orbital eccentricity also evolves throughout the inspiral and approaches unity in the zero-frequency limit for all binaries, making it unsuitable as a common reference point for population analyses. On the other hand, the Newtonian orbital angular momentum is an asymptotic constant of motion of the relativistic two-body problem and remains finite in this limit. In this paper, we make use of this known asymptotic behavior to reformulate eccentric population inference in terms of orbital angular momentum rather than eccentricity and demonstrate this approach on simulated gravitational-wave data. Our work constitutes the first example of eccentric population inference using only asymptotic constants of motion. Importantly, after the inference has been performed using this consistent reference, the results can be propagated to any preferred frequency for comparison with astrophysical predictions.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 6 figures

papers.t: Eccentricity detectability in Extreme Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.abs: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector LISA. Their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. However, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. In this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total SNR of $50$. Eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. In noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total SNR avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. We apply the framework to two astrophysical EMRI populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. The balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future EMRI search developments.
papers.comment: Submitted to Physical Review D. 30 pages, 20 figures

papers.t: Quasars as a self-sufficient probe of the distance duality relation
papers.abs: The distance duality relation links luminosity and angular diameter distances under standard photon propagation. It is usually tested by combining distances from different probes, which requires matching their redshifts and assuming sky isotropy. Self-sufficient probes, which measure both distances for the same object, avoid the first requirement and make the second testable. We assess whether quasars can serve as such probes, combining luminosity distances from the UV--X-ray relation with angular diameter distances from spectroastrometry and reverberation mapping (SARM). As a proof-of-concept, we apply the test to the quasar Mrk~509 and find $η\equiv d_{\rm L}/[(1+z)^2d_{\rm A}] = 0.50^{+0.61}_{-0.27}$, consistent with no violation at $0.8σ$. We then forecast the number of quasars needed to detect a constant and a linearly redshift-dependent violation, motivated by the findings of Teixeira et al. (2025) with potential implications for the Hubble tension and dark energy. A constant violation, $α_0=-0.075$, equivalent to a recalibration of the SNIa distance scale, could be detected at $3σ$ with 274--840 quasars. Since SARM distances, unlike BAO, do not rely on early-time physics, this would separate an early-time origin of the Hubble tension from a SNIa miscalibration or a distance duality violation. The redshift dependence is harder to detect: 1000 quasars would exclude $η=1$ at $3.4$--$6.6σ$, but detecting the dependence itself requires $2.6\times10^4$--$8\times10^4$. GRAVITY+ could bring quasar tests of a constant violation within reach.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Comments are welcome

papers.t: Unraveling the Magnetic Fields of Starspots with Transit Mapping
papers.abs: Stellar magnetic activity is known to decrease as stars age, but the underlying physical mechanism for this decline remains a key question. Does this evolution occur because individual starspots become magnetically weaker (a change in quality), or because the total area covered by spots diminishes (a change in quantity)? We address this question by synthesizing results from two recent studies that leverage starspot transit mapping of Kepler and CoRoT targets. First, we show that the magnetic field strength of starspots remains consistently high, on a saturation plateau of approximately 3500 G, regardless of stellar age or rotation period. This suggests that the intrinsic quality of spots does not significantly evolve. Second, we demonstrate a strong anticorrelation between starspot area coverage and stellar age, with young stars exhibiting large filling factors (up to 29%) that decrease sharply over time. Our combined results provide compelling evidence that the evolution of stellar magnetic activity is primarily driven by a change in the quantity of magnetic flux emerging on the surface, not by a change in the intrinsic strength of the spots themselves. These findings have direct implications for refining stellar dynamo models and improving age-dating techniques.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures. Published in Proceedings IAU Symposium No. 400, "Solar and Stellar Multi-scale Activity", S. Vargas-Domínguez & J. C. Buitrago-Casas, eds., 2026, pp. 122-128

papers.t: Highly spinning binary black holes: promise and pitfalls for parameterized tests of general relativity
papers.abs: Highly spinning binary black holes exhibit complex inspiral dynamics and offer a powerful opportunity to probe gravity in a stronger-field and more dynamical regime than non-spinning binaries. Gravitational-wave signals from such systems enable stringent parameterized tests of deviations from the source dynamics predicted by general relativity. We show that highly spinning, mass-asymmetric binaries can provide enhanced sensitivity to deviations entering at higher post-Newtonian orders, which remain comparatively poorly constrained. Using NR simulations from the SXS catalog, we first recover the injected signals within general relativity using $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM-SpinTaylor}$, $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPNR}$, and $\texttt{SEOBNRv5PHM}$, finding model-dependent biases in the inferred masses, spins, and spin orientations. We then analyze the same signals with the $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM}$-based inspiral parameterized test of general relativity framework, TIGER, and find that these waveform-systematic biases can lead to apparent deviations from general relativity, which become significant for loud signals. Our results highlight that highly spinning binaries offer powerful tests of higher-order post-Newtonian deviations, but waveform inaccuracies can lead to false signs of new physics.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures
